papers.abstract: To identify predictors of surgical success after pediatric tonsillectomy for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and estimate the degree to which non-random selection into postoperative polysomnography (PSG) distorts outcome associations. Retrospective nested cohort study at a quaternary pediatric center (2016-2024). From 940 children undergoing tonsillectomy for OSA, 389 had preoperative PSG and 174 had both preoperative and postoperative PSG. Inverse probability weighting (IPW) corrected for non-random selection into follow-up PSG. Surgical success was defined as postoperative AHI < 5 events/h. The outcome cohort included 174 children (median age 6.0 years; 62% male; 45% obese; median preoperative AHI 16.5 events/h). Surgical success was achieved in 122 (70.1%). Follow-up PSG was associated with higher preoperative AHI (OR 1.06 per event/h), medical complexity (OR 2.22), and multiple comorbidities (OR 1.86), with good discrimination (AUROC 0.795). In IPW-adjusted analysis, each additional event/h of preoperative AHI was associated with lower odds of surgical success (OR 0.96 per event/h; p < 0.001). The estimated effect of obesity strengthened after weighting (OR 0.53 vs. 0.66 unweighted), though the association did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.15). Children with very severe OSA (AHI > 30) achieved success in only 41.7%. Higher preoperative AHI was associated with lower odds of surgical success after tonsillectomy. The obesity estimate did not reach statistical significance after weighting, but whether this reflects a true absence of effect, limited power, or confounding by AHI severity cannot be determined from this dataset. Children with very severe OSA should be counseled that surgery alone is unlikely curative.

papers.title: Sleep and the Gut-Brain Axis: Bidirectional, Converging Mechanisms Linking Brain Health, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: Sleep and the gastrointestinal (GI) tract interact in a complex and reciprocal relationship, although the molecular and physiological pathways underlying this interaction remain only partially defined. Communication between the central (CNS) and enteric nervous systems (ENS) spans neural, immune, endocrine, and metabolic pathways, including vagal nerve signaling, the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, gut-resident microbiota, and circulating microbial metabolites, such as bile acids with neuroinflammatory or neurotransmitter activity. In this narrative review, we synthesize evidence from animal models, observational cohorts, and intervention trials to map this bidirectional axis, focusing on several underexamined modulatory mechanisms including the interaction between the gut microbiome and the glymphatic system, the brain's perivascular waste-clearance network, which is implicated in the removal of amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau in Alzheimer's disease; neuroendocrine regulation and sex-related differences in gut microbiome composition and sleep patterns, which may help explain the divergent neurodegenerative disease risks between men and women; and age-related parallel trajectories of microbiome senescence and sleep fragmentation in older adults. We discuss melatonin, cortisol, estrogen, and ghrelin as endocrine mediators linking circadian biology to gut physiology, and we consider how environmental and lifestyle factors further perturb this system. These mechanisms form an integrative framework of the gut-brain-sleep axis and highlight priority directions for mechanistic and translational research, including significant nodes in this pathway where targeted interventions may help cognitive resilience and slow the neurodegenerative disease progression. More research clarifying these mechanisms may help identify the most promising targets, potentially leading to personalized, precision-medicine-based therapeutic strategies.
papers.journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology

papers.title: Refractory Multivessel Coronary Artery Spasm Unresponsive to Renal Sympathetic Denervation, with Recurrent Transient ST-Segment Elevation and an Episode of Accelerated Idioventricular Rhythm: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Multivessel coronary artery spasm (CAS) is an uncommon, high-risk form of vasospastic angina that can produce transient ST-segment elevation mimicking acute myocardial infarction. Evidence to guide management when calcium channel blockers and nitrates fail is scarce, and renal sympathetic denervation (RSD) has been reported in very few patients; Case Presentation: A 53-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and dyslipidemia presented with nocturnal chest pain and inferior ST-segment elevation. Coronary angiography showed severe spontaneous spasm of the right coronary and left anterior descending arteries that resolved completely with intracoronary nitrate; the coronary arteries were otherwise angiographically normal. High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I remained below 10 ng/L (reference 0-34 ng/L), and echocardiography was normal, fulfilling the criteria for definite vasospastic angina without myocardial infarction. The same two-vessel spasm was documented at a second angiogram three months later. Despite maximally tolerated dual calcium channel blockade, nitrates, and statin therapy, he required more than ten further admissions. A self-terminating accelerated idioventricular rhythm lasting about two minutes was recorded. No syncope or malignant arrhythmia occurred, and an electrophysiology review found no current indication for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. Radiofrequency RSD was performed off-label for refractory symptoms without complications, but at six months, his symptoms and admissions were unchanged; Conclusions: Our case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic difficulties in refractory CAS. Accelerated idioventricular rhythm after relief of spasm is a reperfusion rhythm and does not by itself indicate device therapy. In this patient, RSD did not control refractory multivessel CAS, a negative observation that adds to the very limited evidence on autonomic modulation in this setting.

papers.title: Salivary Cortisol as a Biomarker of Sleep Quality: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Sleep is a crucial regulator for physiological and psychological balance, and sleep disturbances have been associated with the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis. Cortisol exhibits a circadian rhythm and plays a central role in stress response and metabolic regulation. Salivary cortisol has been widely used as a non-invasive biomarker for sleep quality, but its reflection remains unclear. This scoping review aims to systematically map and evaluate the existing literature on the relationship between salivary cortisol and sleep outcomes. Medline, Scopus, and Cochrane databases were applied to identify relevant studies. Database searches combined specific terms from three concept groups: cortisol, sleep quality, and biomarkers. This protocol follows the JBI guidelines. To be incorporated, records pertaining to any type of study design that mentions the use of salivary cortisol and the analysis of sleep quality were considered. Finally, 1067 studies were imported. Among those, 31 studies met eligibility criteria and were extracted. The results indicated the trend in the use of salivary cortisol as a sleep quality biomarker; the study shows limited consistency as a biomarker. Its relationship with sleep outcomes is highly dependent on methodological factors and contextual influences. Overall, salivary cortisol may reflect broader stress-related physiological processes rather than sleep quality directly.

papers.title: Chrononutrition, Dietary Patterns, and Sleep: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence and Practical Implications.
papers.abstract: Sleep and nutrition are closely interconnected through behavioral, metabolic, and circadian pathways, yet the strength of evidence varies considerably across dietary exposures. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on nutrients, foods, dietary patterns, chrononutrition, caffeine and alcohol in relation to sleep, while also considering the effects of insufficient sleep on dietary intake and metabolic health. The relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by examination of reference lists and targeted searches. Higher-quality dietary patterns, particularly Mediterranean-style diets, are generally associated with more favorable sleep characteristics, although predominantly observational evidence limits causal interpretation. Intervention studies of individual foods and supplements have reported benefits for selected sleep outcomes, but findings remain heterogeneous and are often based on small samples. Evidence for meal timing and time-restricted eating is similarly inconsistent and does not support a single eating schedule for improving sleep. In contrast, caffeine and alcohol have relatively well-established sleep-disrupting effects. Insufficient sleep can also alter dietary intake, energy balance, glucose regulation, and adiposity, highlighting the bidirectional nature of these relationships. Nutritional approaches may complement broader strategies for sleep and health, but current evidence does not support specific foods, supplements, or eating schedules as stand-alone treatments for sleep problems.

papers.title: Chronobioethics for Circadian Medicine: Promoting Cardiovascular Health.
papers.abstract: Ambulatory blood pressure (BP) and heart rate (HR) monitoring (ABPM) was performed to investigate the involvement of biological clocks in vascular aging cross-sectionally in 625 citizens (368 women, aged 23-79 years) and longitudinally in 15 citizens (12 women; mean age of 59.3 years) who underwent repeat ABPM after 6.3 years. Vascular aging, estimated by systolic BP (SBP) and pulse pressure (PP), increased with age (p < 0.0001), with a steeper increase at night than during the daytime (0.3362 vs. 0.2765 mmHg/year). Day-to-day variability in morning and evening home SBP also increased with age (p = 0.0127 and 0.0137, respectively). An intensified biological clock mode emerged nonlinearly with age and may protect against early vascular aging. Variance transposition, defined as a shift in the dominant biological rhythm from the circadian to another rhythm, also occurred nonlinearly with age. Circadian-to-circasemidian and circadian-to-circaseptan HR variance transpositions were more frequent in younger subjects and preceded circadian acrophase advance, whereas BP variance transposition predominated in older subjects. Subjects with a normal circadian period (23.5-24.5 h) exhibited less frequent HR, SBP, and DBP variance transposition. In conclusion, SBP and PP increased first at night, whereas reinforced biological clocks improved BP profiles and slowed or even reversed vascular aging.
keywords: 7-day/24 h ambulatory BP and HR monitoring

papers.title: Muscular Response in Sleep-Disordered Breathing Patients: New Methods of Assessment and Measurement.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a heterogeneous disorder influenced by both anatomical collapsibility and non-anatomical factors, such as neuromuscular response. Identifying these traits through simplified clinical surrogates is crucial for personalized precision medicine. This exploratory retrospective study evaluated 207 home polygraphy recordings of Italian patients to assess sleep-stage-specific Apnea-Hypopnea Index (REM vs. NREM AHI) as a clinical surrogate indicator of the balance between anatomical collapsibility and neuromuscular compensation. Patients were stratified by severity into simple snorers (AHI < 5 events/h), mild OSA (AHI 5-15 events/h), and severe OSA (AHI > 30 events/h). REM and NREM AHI values were compared and correlated with Apnea Index (AI), Hypopnea Index (HI), body mass index (BMI), and cumulative nocturnal desaturation indices (CT < 90% and T < 90 min). In non-severe patients (simple snorers and mild OSA), REM AHI was significantly higher than NREM AHI (REM/NREM ratio > 1), suggesting relative neuromuscular protection during NREM sleep. Conversely, in severe OSA patients, the REM/NREM ratio progressively decreased and approached unity, with NREM AHI prevailing. Furthermore, NREM predominance was significantly associated with a higher AI and a worse cumulative desaturation indicating a globally more severe disease. A predominance of REM AHI characterizes milder OSA presentations with effective NREM muscular compensation, whereas NREM predominance aligns with an anatomically dominant, severe phenotype. Decomposing AHI into REM and NREM components provides a practical, readily available clinical surrogate to estimate the anatomy-neuromuscular balance and guide PALM-oriented personalized treatments.

papers.title: Longitudinal Changes in Insomnia, Sleep Continuity, and Sleep Timing During Residential Treatment for Eating Disorders: A Six-Month Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Sleep disturbances are a clinically relevant and transdiagnostic dimension of eating disorders (EDs), particularly during adolescence and young adulthood. Although early improvements in insomnia severity during residential treatment have been described, the longitudinal trajectory of sleep disturbances, habitual sleep timing, and eating disorder psychopathology across a six-month residential stay has not been systematically characterised. Methods: This prospective real-world observational study enrolled 30 female adolescents and young adults (aged 14-22 years) in a small exploratory cohort, predominantly with anorexia nervosa (AN; 83.3%) and a minority with bulimia nervosa (BN; 16.7%), all with clinically significant insomnia at admission (Insomnia Severity Index [ISI] > 14). All sleep outcomes were based on subjective self-report; no objective sleep assessment (actigraphy or polysomnography) was available. Participants were consecutively recruited from the Regional Residential Centre for Eating Disorders "Mariconda", ASL Salerno, Italy. Of 38 consecutive admissions assessed for eligibility, 8 were excluded (ISI ≤ 14 at admission: n = 5; incomplete baseline data: n = 3), yielding a final enrolled sample of n = 30. All 30 participants completed the six-month residential programme; no drop-outs occurred. ISI was assessed monthly (T0-T6); PSQI and EDE-Q were assessed at T0, T3, and T6; diary-derived sleep timing (sleep midpoint) was assessed monthly (T0-T6), while diary-derived sleep continuity parameters (SOL, WASO, TST, SE%) were available at T0, T1, T3, and T6. Linear mixed-effects models (LMM) and bootstrap-resampled paired analyses were used. Results: ISI declined progressively from 21.1 ± 2.5 at baseline to 7.4 ± 2.7 at month 6 (Δ = -13.7; 95% CI [-14.4, -13.1]; p < 0.001). By month 6, 56.7% of participants had achieved remission (ISI < 8) and 100% had met response criteria (ΔISI ≤ -8). Sleep midpoint advanced progressively by 86 min over six months (from ~04:41 to ~03:16 after midnight), with no significant association with BMI or pharmacological treatment in linear mixed-effects models. EDE-Q global scores decreased from 4.57 ± 0.49 to 2.06 ± 0.58. Changes in ISI were not correlated with changes in EDE-Q at month 3 (r = 0.042, p = 0.826) but were significantly correlated at month 6 (r = 0.480, p = 0.007). All pharmacological regimens remained stable throughout the six-month observation period. The association between improvement in insomnia severity and eating-disorder psychopathology was not evident at month 3 but emerged at month 6, suggesting that these domains may change at different rates during residential treatment. Given the exploratory nature of the analyses, p-values are reported without adjustment for multiple comparisons and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Conclusions: Across six months of residential treatment, progressive improvements were observed in insomnia severity, subjective sleep continuity, habitual sleep timing, BMI, and eating-disorder psychopathology. In the absence of a control group, spontaneous remission, regression to the mean, and non-specific components of care, including the routinely administered Passiflora incarnata L. adjunct, cannot be individually distinguished as contributors to the observed changes, and these findings should be interpreted within the constraints of an uncontrolled observational design relying on subjective sleep measures. Controlled studies are needed to determine whether these changes are directly attributable to treatment or primarily reflect concurrent weight restoration and clinical improvement.

papers.title: Parental Revenge Bedtime Procrastination and Parent-Child Feeding Interactions in Early Childhood: A Theory-Driven Perspective on an Unstudied Pathway.
papers.abstract: Bedtime procrastination is defined as delaying sleep despite having no external obstacles. It is a well-established marker of impaired self-regulation and contributes to sleep loss, daytime fatigue, and emotional dysregulation. A parental variant of this behavior is termed parental revenge bedtime procrastination (RBP). This behavior is conceptualized as an autonomy-motivated subtype in which caregivers reclaim personal time at night to compensate for daytime caregiving demands. However, parental RBP has received almost no direct empirical attention, particularly regarding its impact on parent-child interaction quality. Concurrently, distinct literatures on parental technoference, sensitivity, and responsive feeding converge on a shared theme. A sleep-deprived, depleted, and phone-absorbed parent may struggle to read and respond to a young child's hunger and satiety cues during meals. Grounding these relational dynamics in classical infant mental health frameworks highlights the developmental stakes of impaired mealtime reciprocity. Key theoretical foundations include Daniel Stern's theory of affective attunement, Infant Research paradigms by Beebe and Tronick, contemporary neurocognitive models, and Irene Chatoor's clinical classification of feeding disorders. To our knowledge, no study has tested this direct chain in children aged 0-3 years. This perspective article maps existing evidence onto a conceptual model linking parental RBP to feeding interaction quality. It identifies empirically supported segments versus inferential links, proposes a concrete research agenda, outlines potential clinical implications, and advocates for the systematic investigation of this pathway.

papers.title: Photic Phase Shifts of the Mouse Circadian Clock Are Defined by Scene Irradiance Across Differences in the Spatial Distribution of Light.
papers.abstract: Light resets the mammalian circadian clock, but whether this response is determined solely by integrated light intensity (irradiance) or is also influenced by the spatial distribution of light remains unclear. We tested whether high-contrast or low-spatial-frequency patterns modulate circadian responses in mice independently of scene irradiance. Circadian phase shifts were measured following exposure to spatially patterned illumination, including high-contrast checkerboards and spot stimuli positioned at the horizon or zenith. Across all experiments, redistributing light within the visual field did not measurably alter phase-shift amplitude when irradiance was matched between paired conditions. Circadian responses were well predicted by total scene irradiance whereas a metric based on the region of highest radiance provided a poorer account of the data. These findings are consistent with effective spatial integration of light by the mouse circadian system. Within the range of spatial and irradiance conditions tested, our results support irradiance as a simple and effective metric for predicting circadian responses across light environments with divergent spatial distributions.

papers.title: Can Sleep Hypoxic Measures Predict Long-Term Adherence to Positive Airway Pressure Treatments?
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep-related breathing disorder characterized by recurrent upper airway collapse. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is the gold standard treatment but is burdened by low adherence rates. Nighttime hypoxia may alter sleep structure and OSA symptoms, potentially affecting PAP treatment adherence. This study aims to evaluate whether nocturnal hypoxia measures could predict long-term PAP adherence. We conducted a real-life, retrospective study including 207 OSA patients. Clinical data were collected on symptoms, comorbidities, home sleep apnea test (HSAT) metrics, prescribed therapy and objective adherence data via in-built device software. Nocturnal respiratory failure (NRF) was defined as a total sleep time with SpO2 < 90% (TST90) ≥ 30%. Among the cohort, 119 patients met the criteria for NRF. These patients exhibited higher BMI, more severe OSA and a higher prevalence of COPD compared to those without NRF. At follow-up, patients with NRF demonstrated significantly better treatment adherence and more frequently reported improvement in several daytime and nighttime symptoms. Time-to-event analysis and adjusted multivariable regressions showed a higher probability of good long-term PAP adherence in patients with TST90 ≥ 30%. These findings suggest that prolonged nocturnal hypoxemia may identify a subgroup of patients more likely to maintain long-term PAP treatment.

papers.title: Mapping Retinal Gene Expression to Cell Classes: Insights into Retinal Circadian Rhythms.
papers.abstract: Many retinal processes are regulated by circadian rhythms. Previous studies have identified genes with rhythmic retinal expression over a 24 h cycle, but the cell class specificity of many of these genes remains unknown. Here we present a mathematical model, based on existing human retinal single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data and validated using known retinal markers, which assigns cell classes to genes showing uniquely enriched expression in that class. This model assigns retinal cell class specificity to over 10,000 human genes and provides potential novel candidates for retinal cell markers. Additionally, the model enables transcriptomic datasets to be investigated through cell class enrichment analysis. We apply this model to circadian-expressed genes from published mouse ocular transcriptomic data. Specific cell classes were assigned to over 35% of these genes, many of which have little to no previous literature denoting their retinal localisation and role. We also demonstrate significant enrichment of photoreceptor-associated transcripts, many of which are associated with phototransduction and outer segment turnover. The methods and data presented here provide a resource for researchers interested in the cell class specific expression of retinal genes and provide new insight into the cellular basis of retinal circadian rhythms.

papers.title: The Circadian Clock in Glioblastoma: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive brain cancer in adults. Circadian rhythms regulate the sleep-wake cycle, which influences the body's physiological functions. Disruption of circadian rhythms is associated with certain neurological diseases, including GBM. The present narrative review highlights the relationship between circadian rhythm and GBM, the related mechanisms, and the therapeutic approaches against GBM. It also discusses how alterations in the expression of core circadian genes contribute to glioma genesis, especially GBM, and how restoring normal circadian gene function may suppress GBM progression. Additionally, chronotherapy could be considered a potential therapeutic approach for GBM. Aligning chemotherapy and radiotherapy with the internal clock of each patient may have the potential to increase the efficacy of treatments. A better understanding of the potential mechanisms underlying the association between circadian rhythm and GBM pathogenesis may help guide future circadian-based therapeutic approaches; however, further investigation is required.

papers.title: Dietary Approaches to Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Translating Mechanistic Pathways into Clinical Practice.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a highly prevalent and heterogeneous sleep disorder characterized by recurrent upper airway collapse during sleep, resulting in intermittent hypoxia, sleep fragmentation, sympathetic activation, and increased cardiometabolic risk. Although obesity is the most recognized modifiable risk factor, growing evidence indicates that nutritional factors influence OSA through mechanisms extending beyond body weight regulation, including systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, gut microbiota alterations, and metabolic dysregulation. The emergence of precision medicine and incretin-based therapies has further highlighted the need to integrate personalized nutritional approaches into OSA management. A literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify experimental studies, observational studies, randomized clinical trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and international clinical guidelines addressing nutritional mechanisms, dietary patterns, gut microbiota, chrononutrition, incretin-based therapies, and precision nutrition in adults with OSA. Current evidence suggests that nutritional interventions may influence OSA through multiple biological pathways beyond weight reduction. Mediterranean and DASH dietary patterns are associated with favorable cardiometabolic effects, while dietary fiber, polyphenols, omega-3 fatty acids, and other antioxidant compounds may modulate pathways related to inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial function, and metabolic regulation. However, evidence directly demonstrating improvements in objective respiratory outcomes remains limited and heterogeneous. Emerging research also suggests potential roles for gut microbiota modulation and chrononutrition in metabolic and sleep regulation, although most evidence remains mechanistic, observational, or indirect. In addition, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual incretin agonists have demonstrated clinically relevant reductions in body weight and OSA severity, providing opportunities for integration with nutritional management. Nevertheless, evidence supporting phenotype-specific and biomarker-guided nutritional interventions remains insufficient. Nutrition represents a promising adjunctive strategy in the multidisciplinary management of OSA by targeting inflammatory, metabolic, vascular, and microbiome-related mechanisms that extend beyond weight loss alone. Future research should focus on precision nutrition approaches integrating metabolic phenotyping, biomarkers, gut microbiota, and digital health technologies to optimize personalized treatment and improve long-term clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Implementation of a WatchPAT-Based Diagnostic Pathway for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in a Tertiary Hypertension Center: A Feasibility Study.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent yet underdiagnosed in hypertension, affecting 30% to 83% of patients. Limited polysomnography access delays diagnosis. We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and downstream management decisions of an integrated diagnostic pathway using WatchPAT 300, a peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test, in a tertiary hypertension unit. In this single-center, prospective, observational study, 200 patients underwent ambulatory OSA assessment from May 2023 through August 2025. We recorded clinical variables, peripheral arterial tonometry data, and management decisions. A subgroup underwent confirmatory in-laboratory polysomnography. Patients were classified as none-to-mild OSA (peripheral apneahypopnea index <15/h) and moderate-to-severe OSA (≥15/h). The pathway achieved 97.5% (95% CI, 94%-99%) technical success and reduced the mean time-to-diagnosis to 3.5±4.5 days, versus 154 days for in-laboratory polysomnography. Over half of the cohort was triaged: ∼30% met treatment criteria directly, and 22% were ruled out. Among patients completing confirmatory polysomnography, 83% (95% CI, 61%-94%) initially classified as none-to-mild were reclassified as moderate-to-severe OSA, and 77% required treatment. Furthermore, symptoms were dissociated from severity, and Snoring-Tired-Observed-Pressure-BMI-Age-Gender (STOP-Bag) association with severity did not remain significant after multiplicity correction. A peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test-first model is feasible and efficient, eliminating diagnostic delays. Although effective for triaging clear-cut cases, the high reclassification rate underscores the almost mandatory role of confirmatory polysomnography for milder or equivocal results, suspected comorbid sleep disorders, or high STOP-Bag score. These data argue against symptoms-based screening alone to screen populations with hypertension.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association

papers.title: Maxillomandibular Advancement Guided by the Barcelona Line, a Facial Soft-Tissue Reference, in Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Feasibility Study.
papers.abstract: Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) represents an effective surgical treatment for individuals with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) when conservative therapies fail. However, variability in surgical planning methods limits predictability and standardization of outcomes. This retrospective cohort study evaluated clinical and polysomnographic outcomes of MMA planned using the Barcelona Line (BL), and to explore the relationship between BL-guided skeletal positioning and treatment response in adult patients with moderate to severe OSA. Twenty-six consecutive patients (N = 26) underwent standardized virtual planning, surgery, and follow-up, with preoperative and postoperative polysomnography and three-dimensional CBCT analysis. Skeletal movements, upper airway changes, and sleep-related outcomes were assessed. Mean advancement at pogonion was 19.0 ± 4.7 mm. The apnea-hypopnea index decreased significantly from 45.8 ± 11.6 to 6.6 ± 6.6 events/h (mean relative reduction of 85.6 ± 10.9%). Treatment success was achieved in 25/26 patients (96.2%; 95% CI 81.1-99.3) and cure in 22/26 patients (84.6%; 95% CI 66.5-93.9). Daytime sleepiness improved, with ESS scores decreasing from 12.2 ± 1.2 to 1.5 ± 0.4. Total upper airway volume increased from 26.46 ± 2.88 mm3 to 45.32 ± 5.41 mm3. BL-guided MMA is a feasible planning approach associated with substantial clinical improvement in selected OSA patients. The results likely reflect a combination of surgical advancement magnitude and patient selection. Comparative studies are required to determine the independent contribution of the BL.

papers.title: Multidimensional sleep health: risk of cardiovascular disease and mortality, and mediation by plasma proteins.
papers.abstract: Sleep health is a recognised determinant of cardiovascular health, but most previous research has examined individual sleep traits in relation to cardiovascular disease and mortality. The molecular pathways linking multidimensional sleep health to these outcomes remain insufficiently explored. We aimed to examine these associations and identify circulating proteins showing potential mediation signals in these relationships. We analysed data on 257,509 individuals from the UK Biobank, including 26,984 with available plasma proteomic data. Using baseline questionnaire data collected by UK Biobank, we calculated a seven-component sleep health score (SHS) and derived data-driven sleep patterns using K-prototypes clustering. We used multivariable Cox proportional hazards models to examine the associations of the SHS and, separately, the sleep patterns with incident coronary heart disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation and heart failure, as well as cardiovascular and overall mortality. Lastly, we identified SHS-related proteins using linear regression, with representative proteins selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, and mediation analyses performed. Higher SHS was associated with lower risks of coronary heart disease, stroke, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, cardiovascular mortality, and overall mortality, with the strongest associations observed for heart failure and coronary heart disease. Mixed sleep disturbance and non-restorative sleep patterns were associated with higher risks across multiple outcomes. Proteomic analyses identified 188 SHS-related proteins, mainly enriched in inflammatory, immune, and chemotactic pathways. Exploratory mediation analyses identified 34 proteins with potential mediation signals, among which HGF, IGF2R, and FABP4 showed recurrent cross-outcome signals. Poor multidimensional sleep health was associated with higher cardiovascular disease and mortality risks, with exploratory proteomic analyses suggesting potential involvement of circulating proteins related to inflammation, immunity, chemotaxis, and metabolic dysregulation. These findings support multidimensional sleep assessment as a population-level prevention strategy and provide candidate molecular pathways for future mechanistic and interventional studies.

papers.title: Stability of the Epileptogenic Index across seizures and the effects of sleep and withdrawal of anti-seizure medications.
papers.abstract: Epileptogenic Index (EI) is a promising index to evaluate the epileptogenicity of the brain tissue and is useful in planning epilepsy surgery. We aimed to evaluate whether EI maps are consistent across seizures within patients and whether EI-derived measures are affected by the vigilance state and anti-seizure medication (ASM) dose. We analyzed 127 stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) seizures from 19 patients. EI was calculated in all seizures. Within-patient EI consistency was assessed using pairwise Spearman correlations between seizure-specific EI maps. To assess the effects of vigilance and ASM on EI consistency, we calculated a contact-level p_weighted EI score that combines the frequency of suprathreshold EI involvement and mean EI magnitude, separately across vigilance states and in a subset of patients with different ASM states. Mean seizure-to-seizure EI correlations ranged from 0.11 to 0.81, indicating substantial variability in within-patient EI consistency. Seven patients showed high consistency (≥0.6) and four showed low consistency (≤0.3). At the contact level, no differences in p_weighted EI were found between wakefulness and sleep. In contrast, p_weighted EI was significantly higher during reduced ASM compared with full ASM doses. EI maps are not uniformly stable across seizures. ASM reduction may broaden or intensify EI-defined epileptogenic involvement, suggesting that ASM status should be considered when interpreting EI during SEEG evaluation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation to determine their clinical utility for surgical planning. The Epileptogenic Index (EI) measures the involvement of a recorded brain area during a specific seizure. This study shows that EI patterns can vary significantly between different seizures in the same patient. While sleep states do not change these patterns, reducing a patient's anti-seizure medications increases EI values, making seizures appear to spread more broadly. These medication-induced changes must be carefully considered to accurately map the epileptic network for surgical decisions.

papers.title: Beauty of ambiguity in the eye of the night owl: Morningness-eveningness preference is associated with tolerance of ambiguity.
papers.abstract: Prior work has robustly linked eveningness, a preference for later sleep and activity timing, to distinct personality profiles, such as openness to experience and divergent thinking. In turn, these individual differences have been associated with individuals' ability to navigate uncertain situations. Synthesizing these lines of evidence, we hypothesized that eveningness, as assessed by the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (MEQ), would be positively associated with tolerance of ambiguity. We tested this hypothesis across three methodologically complementary studies (N = 835) that incorporated samples from two cultural contexts (Chinese and Laotian) and multiple measures of tolerance of ambiguity (self-report and behavioral indices). In Study 1, we provided preliminary evidence that individuals with a stronger evening preference exhibited higher levels of tolerance of ambiguity in a sample of Chinese university students. To increase the generalizability of our findings, we sampled Laotian community adults in Study 2 and successfully replicated the observed relationship. Finally, moving beyond self-report measures, Study 3 provided convergent behavioral evidence for the association in a Chinese non-student sample. Taken together, these findings, which replicate across two cultural contexts, extend research on morningness-eveningness beyond the traditional domains of sleep, affect, and performance by identifying tolerance of ambiguity as a novel psychological correlate of eveningness.

papers.title: Determination of sleep quality and factors affecting on nursing students: A cross-sectional survey research in Iraq.
papers.abstract: Total sleep duration, onset latency, sleep efficiency, and other factors are frequently used to define the quality of sleep. Sleep disturbances are a prevalent health issue that is predicted to increase and have more significant effects on adults, particularly on medical students, specifically nursing students. Additionally, we have a few studies on sleep quality that we have documented. The objective of the study to determine the factors affecting nursing Students' sleep quality. The study uses a cross-sectional methodology and an analytical-observational research design. The population of 840 students enrolled in the first morning study session of the 2024-2025 academic year at Mosul University Faculty/College of Nursing/Department of Clinical Sciences Nursing served as the research sample for this descriptive and cross-sectional study. In total, 350 students who volunteered for the study make up the sample. The study's instruments are divided into two categories: Initial sections, such demographics characteristics. In part two, the Pittsburg Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) questionnaire. A P value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The analysis was conducted using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences. The results of the current study showed that students aged (20-23) are the most likely to suffer from sleep quality disorders, at a rate of 76%. The average sleep duration among most students was less than 6 hours, at a rate of 77.14%. In general, nursing students have poor sleep quality, according to the study's findings. Less than six hours of sleep per day is the norm for students. Additionally, students who abstain from smoking, get more than eight hours of sleep each day, and limit their intake of caffeinated beverages like tea and coffee sleep better.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion

papers.title: Anthropometric profile, hypertension, and lifestyle risk factors: A cross-sectional study among Kurdish medical students.
papers.abstract: Medical students, as future healthcare professionals, should model healthy lifestyle behaviors. However, their own practices and health profiles often fall short of optimal standards. This study assessed anthropometric measures, lifestyle habits, and clinical risk factors for non-communicable diseases among Kurdish medical students. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 280 undergraduate medical students (80 males, 200 females) aged 18-24 years at Hawler Medical University. Data were collected using a two-part approach: (1) direct clinical assessments for anthropometrics (height, weight), blood pressure (BP), and random blood glucose (RBG); and (2) a pre-validated, structured questionnaire to document diet, physical activity, smoking, and sleep patterns. Body Mass Index (BMI) was calculated and categorized. Gender-based differences and correlations were analyzed. A normal BMI was observed in 59.3% of students; however, 22.1% were overweight, 8.6% obese, and 10% underweight. Hypertension prevalence was high (56.4%), while most participants had normal RBG (92.9%). Male students had significantly higher BMI, SBP, DBP, and less healthy dietary habits compared to females (P < 0.001). Positive correlations were found between BMI and both Systolic Blood Pressure (SBP) (r = 0.30) and Diastolic Blood Pressure (DBP) (r = 0.22), but not with Random Blood Glucose (RBG). High BMI was also associated with hypertension and poor sleep. Despite most students having a normal BMI, a substantial proportion exhibited elevated blood pressure, overweight, and obesity, underscoring the need for targeted lifestyle interventions and health promotion within medical education.
papers.journal: Journal of education and health promotion

papers.title: Sleep inertia, daytime sleepiness, and falls in older adults of the Wisconsin Sleep Cohort.
papers.abstract: Examine associations between sleep inertia, daytime sleepiness, and falls in older adults of the Wisconsin Sleep Cohort (WSC). Cross-sectional data from WSC participants were used. Participants completed the Sleep Inertia Questionnaire (SIQ) and Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). Elevated sleep inertia (ESI) was defined as the upper quartile (SIQ > 37), while ESS > 10 defined excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS). Falls outcomes included self-reported recurrent (<2 vs 2+) and injurious (no vs yes) falls over the previous year. Logistic regressions examined associations with falls outcomes. Fully adjusted analyses included demographics and outcome-specific sleep, psychiatric, medical, physical, and cognitive covariates. Secondary analyses explored associations with SIQ subscales. The recurrent falls sample included 392 older adults (74.5 ± 6.6 years; 44.9% female), while 162 participants with ≥1 fall comprised the injurious falls sample (75.4 ± 6.6 years; 45.1% female). In unadjusted analyses, higher SIQ scores and ESI were significantly associated with recurrent and injurious falls; however, in fully adjusted analyses, the associations remained significant only for recurrent falls (SIQ: OR = 1.04, 95% CI = 1.00-1.07; ESI: OR = 2.00, 95% CI = 1.07-3.73). Higher ESS scores and EDS were significantly associated with recurrent falls in unadjusted analyses, but not in fully adjusted analyses. Neither ESS nor EDS was associated with injurious falls. In SIQ subscale analyses, Physiological symptoms were most strongly associated with recurrent falls, whereas Cognitive symptoms were most strongly associated with injurious falls. Sleep inertia may represent an important, under-recognized risk factor for falls in older adults.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society

papers.title: Interpreting Cytomegalovirus Seropositivity Beyond the Neonatal Diagnostic Window: A Case Report on an Infant With Early-Onset Atopic Dermatitis and Congenital Arthrogryposis.
papers.abstract: Congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) infection has a broad clinical spectrum and may result in permanent neurological, auditory, visual, and developmental sequelae. We report the case of a six-month-old male infant investigated primarily for microcephaly who had a complex phenotype comprising a cutaneous rash present from birth that evolved into moderate early-onset atopic dermatitis with severe clinical and quality-of-life impairment, growth impairment, congenital arthrogryposis, neonatal jaundice with hyperbilirubinemia, mild neonatal thrombocytopenia, and neurosensory abnormalities. He was born at 36 weeks and four days after reduced amniotic fluid volume was noted at approximately 36 weeks. Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia did not require phototherapy, and a follow-up peripheral blood smear was unremarkable. At six months, the dermatitis consisted of widespread erythematous-squamous, intensely pruritic lesions with facial and periorbital involvement and sleep disturbance. After 40 days of conventional treatment with emollients, skin-barrier care, and topical corticosteroids, the SCORAD (Scoring Atopic Dermatitis) index decreased from 45 to 18, although residual lesions persisted. Growth was impaired, with marked underweight (weight-for-age z-score <-3) and reduced linear growth (length-for-age z-score -2.6), while head circumference was 40.8 cm (z-score -2.2), consistent with microcephaly. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed preserved cerebral architecture with symmetric periventricular and peritrigonal T2 hyperintensity considered indeterminate and potentially related to incomplete physiological myelination. Auditory brainstem evoked responses and visual evoked potentials were abnormal. Creatine kinase was mildly elevated, whereas neurological examination and electromyography were normal. Quantitative immunoglobulins, serum protein electrophoresis, and lymphocyte subset analysis were unremarkable. Maternal CMV-specific IgM and IgG were positive during the eighth month of pregnancy, and the infant had positive CMV-specific IgM and IgG at six months. In the absence of virological testing within the first 21 days of life or an archived neonatal dried blood spot, congenital infection could not be definitively confirmed. This case emphasizes the critical importance of recognizing suggestive neonatal findings and testing for cCMV within the first 21 days of life, particularly in settings where retrospective dried-blood-spot testing is unavailable.

papers.title: Sleep patterns and sleep disorders in pregnant women with preeclampsia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy with diverse and poorly understood risk factors. Hormonal changes during this period affect sleep, raising the question of whether sleep disturbances may be related to PE. This review aimed to investigate the prevalence of sleep disturbances among pregnant women diagnosed with PE. We included observational studies and clinical trials assessing sleep by any method. Exclusion criteria were studies on PE without sleep assessment, systematic reviews, editorials, animal studies, and unavailable full texts. Studies were retrieved from Virtual Health Library, MEDLINE and Embase using the descriptors "preeclampsia" and "sleep" with additional manual searches. The last search was conducted on December 10, 2024. Screening and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Risk of bias was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Random-effects models were used to synthesize prevalence as proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Twenty-one studies were included from 2,075 initially identified. The pooled prevalence of sleep disturbances in PE was 46% (95% CI [0,19 - 0,76]), p=0,823. Stratified analysis identified two categories: qualitative disturbances, with prevalence of 50% (95% CI [0.31-0.70]); and sleep-disordered breathing with prevalence of 43% (95% CI [0.10-0.83]). This meta-analysis found an estimated 46% prevalence of sleep disturbances in preeclampsia; however, the evidence is of very low quality (GRADE), due to extreme heterogeneity and uncontrolled risk of bias.PROSPERO: CRD42024557766.
papers.journal: Revista brasileira de ginecologia e obstetricia : revista da Federacao Brasileira das Sociedades de Ginecologia e Obstetricia

papers.title: Case Report: Application of the 6D BTS digital assessment system in the comprehensive management of refractory cancer pain in a patient with gallbladder carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cancer pain is a major complication that adversely affects the quality of life of cancer patients, with approximately 10%-20% of patients developing refractory cancer pain that conventional medications fail to control. Traditional unidimensional assessment tools cannot fully capture the complexity of this condition. We therefore applied a novel digital tool, the 6D BTS (Botong score) digital assessment system, which was integrated with a robotic device. This system provided a multidimensional, objective evaluation through a digital interface, assessing pain intensity, physical function, emotional status, sleep quality, neuropathic pain, and breakthrough pain. The system also enabled remote dynamic monitoring outside the hospital. We report a case of gallbladder carcinoma with clavicular metastasis and recurrent sternal pain. Using a robotic system integrated with the BTS system, we conducted a comprehensive assessment of the patient's pain. Based on the detailed information provided by the BTS system, we designed a personalized analgesic plan that controlled the cancer pain to some extent: the patient's Numeric Rating Scale score decreased from 8 to 1, and breakthrough pain episodes dropped from 6 times per day to 0. We conclude that the BTS system offers an effective digital solution for the comprehensive management of refractory cancer pain.

papers.title: Everyday discrimination alters cognitive benefits of restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep in Black adults.
papers.abstract: Restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep has been linked to cognitive functioning. Yet, it remains unclear whether experiences of discrimination, a persistent form of identity-based adversity, shape how objectively measured restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep relates to cognitive outcomes in Black Americans. Ninety-two Black adults completed the Everyday Discrimination Scale, a cognitive assessment, and three nights of at-home sleep monitoring. Restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep was indexed using N2-N3 delta power. Moderation analyses evaluated whether everyday discrimination altered the association between restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep and global cognition, assessed with the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, as well as visuospatial memory, assessed with the Benson Complex Figure task, adjusting for age, sex, marital status, education, subjective socioeconomic status, body mass index, and sleep efficiency. Discrimination moderated the relationship between restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep and global cognition. At lower levels of discrimination, greater levels of restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep corresponded to higher global cognition scores, whereas at higher levels of discrimination, a greater level of restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep corresponded to lower global cognition scores. The interaction between restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep and discrimination on visuospatial memory was not significant after full covariate adjustment, with education emerging as a significant independent predictor of visuospatial memory. The findings suggest that associations between restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep and global cognition vary across levels of everyday discrimination among Black adults, independent of socioeconomic and health-related factors. These results highlight discrimination as a relevant contextual factor to consider when examining sleep-cognition relationships in cognitive aging.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society

papers.title: P waves marching through QRS during supraventricular tachycardia: What is the mechanism?
Usher Syndrome Type 2A and Epileptic Encephalopathy with Spike-Wave Activation in Sleep: A Coincidental Dual Diagnosis? Case Report.
papers.abstract: USH2A-related Usher syndrome type 2A is classically characterized by congenital or early-onset sensorineural hearing loss and later-onset retinitis pigmentosa, and epilepsy is not a recognized feature of USH2A-related disease. We report an 11-year-old boy who initially presented with nocturnal focal seizures and left occipital epileptiform discharges, followed by cognitive and academic decline and an electroencephalographic evolution consistent with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep (EE-SWAS). Brain magnetic resonance imaging, including repeat evaluation with 3-Tesla imaging, was normal. Because of known parental consanguinity and a treatment-resistant course, exome sequencing was performed and identified a homozygous pathogenic USH2A variant, USH2A(NM_206933.4):c.802G>A;p.(Gly268Arg), with heterozygous segregation in both parents. Genotype-directed evaluation confirmed bilateral moderate-to-moderately severe sensorineural hearing loss (pure tone average: right 60 dB HL; left 50 dB HL), whereas retinal involvement was not clinically evident at the time of assessment. To our knowledge, the co-occurrence of biallelic USH2A pathogenicity and an EE-SWAS phenotype has not been reported previously. However, because the same USH2A variant has not been associated with epilepsy or EE-SWAS in the published literature, this co-occurrence is most plausibly interpreted as a coincidental dual diagnosis/dual pathology. This case is noteworthy because it illustrates that exome sequencing may uncover unexpected but clinically actionable syndromic diagnoses and guide targeted audiologic and ophthalmologic surveillance planning, even when the presenting phenotype is primarily neurologic.
keywords: Epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep

papers.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder with comorbid obstructive sleep apnea after the Great East Japan Earthquake: A case report.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is frequently accompanied by sleep disturbance, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is an important potential comorbidity. Although PTSD-OSA coexistence has been reported mainly in military veterans, reports after natural disasters remain limited. We describe a patient who developed PTSD after the Great East Japan Earthquake (GEJE) and was subsequently diagnosed with severe OSA. A 55-year-old man with hypertension and dyslipidemia, but no prior psychiatric illness, experienced temporary burial under rubble during the GEJE. He subsequently developed persistent trauma-related nightmares, depressed mood, and panic responses to disaster-related cues and was diagnosed with PTSD. Paroxetine and alprazolam improved mood and panic symptoms, whereas nightmares, excessive daytime sleepiness, and impaired concentration persisted. Polysomnography later demonstrated severe OSA (apnea-hypopnea index, 41.6 events/h; rapid eye movement (REM) AHI, 47.6 events/h; minimum oxygen saturation, 79%). Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was initiated without changes to psychiatric treatment. Daytime sleepiness improved, and nightmare frequency decreased from almost daily to approximately weekly during the period of CPAP treatment, although adherence was low and symptoms later recurred after treatment interruption. This case illustrates that persistent nightmares, sleepiness, and impaired daytime functioning in a patient with PTSD may coexist with clinically significant OSA. Because longitudinal standardized PTSD measures were unavailable and CPAP adherence was limited, the observed improvement cannot be attributed to CPAP alone. Systematic assessment for sleep disorders, including OSA, should be considered when sleep-related or daytime symptoms persist during psychiatric treatment.
papers.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences

papers.title: Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation in a Pacemaker-Dependent Child with Syndromic Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: A Case Report with Prospective 9-Month Follow-Up.
papers.abstract: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is an emerging noninvasive neuromodulation therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE). However, evidence regarding its use in patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices, particularly pacemaker-dependent children, remains extremely limited. We report a 6-year-old boy with genetically confirmed TAF6-related Alazami-Yuan syndrome, severe developmental impairment, complete atrioventricular block requiring permanent epicardial VVIR pacing, and syndromic DRE refractory to multiple antiseizure medications (ASMs). Auricular taVNS was initiated at the cymba conchae under multidisciplinary supervision using stimulation parameters of 25 Hz, pulse width 250 μs, intensity titrated to tolerance up to 1.7 mA, for 4 h/day. Treatment initiation was performed in the pediatric intensive care unit with continuous electrocardiographic monitoring for 5 days. The patient underwent prospective follow-up over 9 months using caregiver-maintained seizure diaries, serial electroencephalography (EEG), serial electrocardiography, repeated pacemaker interrogation, adverse event surveillance, and Pediatric Quality of Life Family Impact Module (PedsQL-FIM) assessments. No arrhythmias, pacing abnormalities, device malfunction, or clinically significant pacemaker parameter changes were observed during follow-up. A mild transient local skin irritation resolved with conservative care. Seizure burden decreased from 2 to 4 prolonged seizures daily at baseline to approximately two brief generalized tonic seizures weekly, with sustained improvement through month 9. Reduction of ASM burden began only after clinical improvement had already been observed. Follow-up EEGs remained markedly abnormal with only limited interval electrographic change. PedsQL-FIM improved progressively from 10.4 at baseline to 54.9 at month 3, 80.6 at month 7, and 84.0 at month 9. Auricular taVNS was successfully administered in a pacemaker-dependent child under structured multidisciplinary monitoring without identifiable cardiac or pacemaker-related adverse events during 9 months of follow-up. Although efficacy and safety conclusions cannot be inferred from a single case, this report supports the clinical feasibility of combining noninvasive vagal neuromodulation with permanent cardiac pacing in carefully selected pediatric patients.

papers.title: Real time quantification of carbohydrates in beer wort by FTIR and neural network analysis.
papers.abstract: The brewing process of wort has been predominantly empirical, once that just after the production of a batch is possible to evaluate the performance of raw materials, and if its necessary makes adjustments for the next batches. In this context, the real time information about the composition of the beer wort can facilitate the implemention of modifications during the process to improve both efficiency and precision of the desired physicochemical profile. Thus, this work shows the development of an equipment and signal processing that combines three techniques for monitoring the mashing process in beer production. Real-time quantification of carbohydrates produced by enzymatic reactions between barley malt enzymes and starch during the saccharification step, which is usually achieved through spectral analysis using Fourier transform infrared absorption in the mid-infrared region through collection and referring samples in real time. The system incorporates principal component analysis and artificial neural networks for data processing, however by implementing a flow measurement system controlled by software, the concentration of major carbohydrates (glucose, maltose, maltotriose, and dextrins) in the wort can be quantified during the enzymatic reactions in real time. These measurements offer new possibilities for process control, error reduction, and optimization of reactions as needed, allowing fine control of the process. The real time spectroscopy will provide the application of machine learning tools in the process. While the device and procedure is demonstrated for the efficient control of the beer production, its context and applicability goes much beyond such applications. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13197-024-06128-4.
papers.journal: Journal of food science and technology

papers.title: A screening method for aortic valve disease based on spectral analysis of a single-channel electrocardiogram using machine learning algorithms.
papers.abstract: Given the high prevalence of aortic heart disease and the importance of early diagnosis, there is a need to develop a simple screening method to identify significant aortic heart disease based on available biosignals, one of which is a single-channel electrocardiogram (ECG). We aimed to develop a machine learning algorithm for analyzing single-channel electrocardiograms to identify patients with moderate to severe aortic stenosis and regurgitation, as well as significant aortic valve disease. Patients (n = 2,503) underwent echocardiographic examination and single-channel I-lead ECG recording using a portable electrocardiograph. Moderate to severe aortic stenosis on echocardiography was present in 62 (2.4%) patients, and moderate to severe aortic regurgitation was present in 157 (6.3%). Single-channel ECG analysis was performed using advanced signal processing and machine learning techniques. Both models were evaluated under an identical 10-fold group cross-validation framework. For detecting moderate or severe aortic stenosis, diagnostic accuracy was 0.650 (Se 57.9%, Sp 65.0%) for Balanced Random Forest and 0.662 (Se 46.4%, Sp 66.5%) for XGBoost. For moderate or severe aortic regurgitation, accuracy was 0.726 (Se 60.5%, Sp 73.3%) for Balanced Random Forest and 0.712 (Se 61.7%, Sp 71.9%) for XGBoost. For significant aortic valve disease, accuracy was 0.724 (Se 61.1%, Sp 73.4%) for Balanced Random Forest and 0.691 (Se 67.8%, Sp 69.2%) for XGBoost. The results indicate good diagnostic accuracy and potential applicability for screening for significant aortic heart disease using single-channel ECG parameters analyzed with modern signal processing and machine learning techniques.Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrial.gov/, identifier NCT07099417.

papers.title: Parathyroid Storm Secondary to a Parathyroid Adenoma Presenting With Recurrent Generalised Tonic-Clonic Seizures and Refractory Hypercalcaemia: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Parathyroid storm is a rare, life-threatening manifestation of primary hyperparathyroidism characterised by severe hypercalcaemia and acute multisystem deterioration. We report a 70-year-old woman with known primary hyperparathyroidism who presented with progressive weakness, confusion and reduced mobility and was found to have a corrected serum calcium concentration of 4.14 mmol/L. Despite aggressive intravenous hydration, she developed recurrent generalised tonic-clonic seizures, hypoventilation and reduced consciousness, requiring intubation and intensive care admission. Electroencephalography demonstrated severe diffuse cerebral dysfunction consistent with metabolic encephalopathy, while cerebrospinal fluid studies were unremarkable. Four-dimensional computed tomography of the neck identified a 1.8 cm right-sided parathyroid lesion. Hypercalcaemia remained difficult to control despite multimodal medical therapy, including pamidronate, calcitonin, cinacalcet and denosumab, with recurrent rebound hypercalcaemia. Urgent parathyroidectomy resulted in sustained normalisation of serum calcium and cessation of seizure activity, and histopathology confirmed a benign parathyroid adenoma. This case highlights the severe neurological complications of parathyroid storm and the importance of early multidisciplinary consideration of definitive surgery when hypercalcaemia remains refractory to intensive medical therapy.

papers.title: Dietary, lifestyle, and host determinants of microbiota-host interactions.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota is a dynamic ecosystem shaped by dietary factors, lifestyle factors, environmental exposures, and host characteristics, with important implications for metabolism, immune regulation, intestinal barrier function, and host-microbiota interactions. This narrative review examines how dietary patterns, specific food components, physical activity, sleep and circadian rhythms, aging, and medication exposure modulate gut microbial composition and function, with particular emphasis on interindividual variability and personalized nutrition. A literature search was conducted in Scopus, ScienceDirect, PubMed, and Google Scholar for publications from 2000 to 2026, with emphasis on recent peer-reviewed evidence. Current evidence indicates that dietary patterns and individual food components can modify microbial community structure, metabolic pathways, and bioactive metabolite production, although responses vary substantially across individuals. Physical activity may modify microbial ecology, intestinal physiology, barrier function, and microbial metabolism, whereas sleep disruption and circadian misalignment may alter microbial rhythmicity and host metabolic regulation. Aging and antibiotic exposure are associated with context-dependent changes in microbial composition, function, resilience, and, with antibiotics, the gut resistome. Across these determinants, interindividual variability emerges as a central feature driven by host characteristics, habitual diet, lifestyle, medication history, baseline microbiota, and microbial functional capacity. Personalized nutrition therefore represents a promising but evolving framework in which microbiome data may be integrated with host and environmental characteristics to predict differential responses. Future research should prioritize longitudinal human studies, standardized methodologies, multi-omics integration, and prospective validation of microbiome-informed interventions to establish clinically meaningful benefits.

papers.title: Psychotic symptoms in tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency-associated dopa-responsive dystonia treated with antipsychotics and rTMS: a case report.
papers.abstract: Tyrosine hydroxylase deficiency (THD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the TH gene. THD encompasses a broad phenotypic spectrum that includes dopamine-responsive dystonia (DRD) as its milder presentation, alongside severe infantile parkinsonism and progressive infantile encephalopathy. Although non-motor manifestations-such as depression, anxiety, and sleep disturbances-have garnered increasing attention, psychotic symptoms including hallucinations and delusions remain rarely reported in THD. This report describes a genetically confirmed woman with THD who presented with infantile-onset dystonia. Auditory hallucinations and erotomanic delusions emerged approximately five years after levodopa initiation and persisted despite one-month levodopa withdrawal. Although levodopa markedly improved her dystonia, antipsychotic treatment posed a therapeutic dilemma: risperidone exacerbated motor symptoms, and aripiprazole was limited by poor adherence. A multimodal regimen comprising aripiprazole, quetiapine, and low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) targeting the left temporoparietal cortex was associated with progressive improvement of psychotic symptoms without clinically apparent worsening of dystonia. The independent contribution of rTMS could not be determined given the concurrent pharmacological titration. Selecting appropriate antipsychotic medication in THD patients with prominent psychotic symptoms poses a considerable challenge. The combination of aripiprazole, quetiapine, and rTMS may represent a potential therapeutic option. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of genetically confirmed DRD due to THD presenting with prominent psychotic symptoms, and among the few documenting rTMS use in this population. These observations are based on clinical assessment without standardized quantitative measures; the independent efficacy of rTMS cannot be established from this case.

papers.title: Immediate anxiety-reducing effects of multisensory virtual reality reminiscence therapy in older adults with a wide range of cognitive functions: a pilot study using electrophysiological measures.
papers.abstract: Anxiety is a prevalent behavioral and psychological symptom of dementia (BPSD) in older adults with cognitive impairment, severely diminishing their quality of life. Although reminiscence therapy (RT) is a promising non-pharmacological intervention, objective neurophysiological methods to evaluate its immediate emotional impact remain unexplored. This pilot study proposed "Smart Reminiscence Therapy (SRT)" - a novel virtual reality (VR) system integrated with synchronized multisensory stimuli - and evaluated its immediate anxiety-reducing effects and the utility of electrophysiological measures. A single-session, single-arm pre-post exploratory design was adopted. Twenty older adults (aged 65 years or older) at a day service center, with Mini-Mental State Examination-Japanese (MMSE-J) scores of 11-30, participated. The intervention consisted of a 10-min SRT session featuring a 1960s Japanese townscape. The primary outcome was objective resting-state eye-closed frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA) via a wearable EEG device, while subjective state anxiety via the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) was evaluated as a secondary outcome. After excluding three participants with excessive artifacts, 17 participants (mean age: 85.9 ± 5.9 years; mean MMSE-J: 23.8 ± 3.8, with 64.7% clustered in the MCI-to-mild-dementia range) were analyzed. Subjective STAI scores showed a non-significant decreasing trend with a moderate effect size (p = 0.088, r = 0.414). Conversely, the FAA index significantly increased post-intervention (p = 0.038, Cohen's d = 0.55). No significant correlation was found between changes in STAI and FAA (r = -0.15, p = 0.562). A single session of SRT was associated with an increase in FAA; however, the uncontrolled design precludes causal attribution to the intervention. The dissociation between subjective reports and neurophysiological changes suggests that FAA may complement self-reported measures by capturing aspects of acute emotional change that may be difficult to verbalize in people with cognitive impairment. The non-significant but moderate-sized reduction in STAI scores warrants confirmation in larger controlled studies.

papers.title: Noninvasive diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease: a review of emerging biomarkers and multimodal approaches.
papers.abstract: Noninvasive biomarkers are expanding access to biological assessment of Alzheimer's disease (AD). This review evaluates blood-based, neuroimaging, retinal, electrophysiological, digital, and behavioral measures alongside structured cognitive and functional assessment, and examines multimodal and machine-learning approaches for detection, differential diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. Plasma phosphorylated tau, particularly p-tau217, currently offers the strongest scalable evidence for identifying amyloid and advanced tau pathology, whereas PET and MRI retain complementary roles in pathological confirmation, regional staging, exclusion of alternative causes, and characterization of atypical phenotypes. Retinal, electrophysiological, speech, sleep, and eye-tracking measures remain promising but require greater standardization and external validation. Across modalities, biomarker trajectories are temporally staggered, assay and platform differences affect interpretation, and pathology-phenotype mapping is modified by disease stage, cognitive reserve, copathology, vascular factors, and population characteristics. We therefore propose a phenotype-anchored, stepped pathway that begins with patient and informant history, objective cognitive and functional assessment, structural imaging, and routine laboratory evaluation; adds validated blood biomarkers when they resolve a defined uncertainty; and reserves CSF or PET for unresolved, atypical, or treatment-relevant cases. Discordant findings should prompt reassessment rather than automatic reclassification. We describe the literature-search and descriptive evidence-categorization approach used to select and categorize the evidence reviewed, and we place the findings within the emerging regulatory context of blood-based testing. Clinical translation will depend on harmonized thresholds, representative prospective cohorts, calibration, independent validation, and evidence that multimodal systems improve decisions and patient outcomes rather than benchmark accuracy alone.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: Early clinical and biologic predictors of dupilumab response in pediatric moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.
papers.abstract: To identify early clinical, inflammatory, and skin barrier-related predictors of dupilumab response in pediatric patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, and to develop a practical early prediction model to stratify short-term therapeutic outcomes, thereby facilitating individualized treatment optimization in routine clinical practice. In this retrospective cohort study, we enrolled 300 consecutive pediatric patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis who initiated dupilumab at the Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, between January 2024 and December 2025. Patients were classified as non-responders (n = 156) or responders (n = 144) according to predefined response criteria during follow-up. The primary outcome was early rapid response by week 16. Baseline demographic, clinical, inflammatory, and skin barrier variables were collected, together with dynamic changes at weeks 2 and 4. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors and construct an Early Clinical-Biologic Prediction Score (CEPS) model. The model's discrimination, subgroup performance, longitudinal interactions, and week-16 risk-stratified outcomes were evaluated. Responders had significantly lower baseline disease severity, inflammatory burden, and barrier dysfunction, with lower Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI) score, SCORing Atopic Dermatitis (SCORAD), pruritus and sleep-loss Numerical Rating Scale (NRS), Patient-Oriented Eczema Measure (POEM), Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI), eosinophil count, and LDH (all P≤0.001). These between-group differences widened over time, as responders showed substantially greater improvement by weeks 2 and 4 across all major clinical and biomarker measures (all P<0.001). By multivariable analysis, the CEPS model showed stable discrimination across prespecified subgroups (AUC range, 0.84-0.89). CEPS-based stratification further identified a clear gradient in week-16 outcomes, including EASI-75/EASI-90 achievement, symptom improvement, barrier recovery, and lower rescue treatment use, unscheduled visits, and treatment intensification (all P<0.001). Early clinical, inflammatory, and skin barrier changes after dupilumab initiation provide robust prediction of subsequent treatment response in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.

papers.title: 2026 Asia Pacific Heart Rhythm Society (APHRS) Guidelines (Part IV) on Comprehensive Lifestyle Risk Factor and Comorbidity Management in Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is closely associated with comorbidities and lifestyle factors that influence the development, progression, and outcomes. Here the focus is on guidelines for the systematic management of hypertension, heart failure, coronary and structural heart disease, diabetes, dyslipidemia, cerebrovascular disease, obesity, chronic kidney disease, thyroid dysfunction, inflammatory disease, cancer and frailty. In addition, it provides guidelines for lifestyle factors such as nutrition, physical activity, alcohol consumption, tobacco use, sleep and psychological health as key components of AF care. Finally, multimorbidity, polypharmacy and the diverse clinical, cultural, socioeconomic and healthcare contexts of the Asia Pacific region are also addressed. Particular focus is driven by evidence to support the comprehensive management of lifestyle factors as a core component of AF care with equitable access adapted to local resources and patient needs.

papers.title: "I feel like I'm in a dream": a qualitative investigation of the lived experience of Visual Snow Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Visual Snow Syndrome (VSS) is neurological condition typified by persistent visual snow, or static, throughout the visual field, alongside additional phenomena that impact night vision, visual perception, and visual processing. Only formally characterized in the 2010s, little consideration has been given to the broader impacts of this condition on the lives of those who experience it. This study presents the first qualitative investigation of the lived experience of Visual Snow Syndrome, to further inform clinical, research, and consumer communities alike. Forty-nine adults who self-identified as having VSS completed an online survey that queried the good and bad aspects of VSS, and its general impact on their daily life. Their qualitative data were analyzed iteratively, to determine the key themes represented across and between individual responses. The lived experience of VSS varied both inter and intra-individually across this sample. Responses endorsed several themes: mental health and psychosocial wellbeing, functional vision, the dynamic course of visual snow syndrome, clinical challenges, and medical system limitations. The majority of participants described their VSS as a negative component of their daily life, with specific descriptions outlining how living with VSS worsened their mental health, cognition, sleep, daily routines, visual quality, and comfort in both natural and artificial light. However, one third of participants were able to identify some positive aspects of their visual snow experience, highlighting that it can bring unique meaning and fascination to their lives. VSS has broad and varied impacts on the day-to-day lives of those who experience it. It can introduce substantial mental health and psychosocial wellbeing challenges and functional vision impairments, but also a unique, and sometimes beautiful perspective. These experiences, paired with its variability between and within persons, indicates a need for more holistic and individualized approaches to the long-term treatments and supports.

papers.title: Epidemiological profile of the homeless population and factors associated with illicit psychoactive substance use: cross-sectional study, Jundiaí, 2023.
papers.abstract: To describe the sociodemographic and clinical-epidemiological characteristics of the homeless population and to assess factors associated with illicit psychoactive substance use in Jundiaí, São Paulo, Brazil, in 2023. : This study employed a cross-sectional design with a homeless population. The outcome was substance use, and the independent variables were grouped into exogenous factors, primary and intermediate health determinants, access to services, health perception, and clinical conditions. Descriptive and bivariate statistical analyses were performed. Odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) were calculated using multiple binary logistic regression. There were 270 participants, the majority of whom were male (85.2%), with an average age of 39, self-identified as Black (72.6%), heterosexual (88.5%), with incomplete elementary education (54.8%), living on the street for five years or more (45.6%), and 80.4% had used/were using illicit psychoactive substances.
