The most prevalent conditions were mental distress (83.0%), sleep problems (77.4%), digestive discomfort (34.8%), and respiratory disease (31.5%). The use of illicit substances was associated with: having completed high school or higher (OR 4.16; 95%CI 1.63; 10.62); living on the streets for more than one year (OR 2.08; 95%CI 1.01; 4.28); having suffered violence (OR 2.05; 95%CI 1.04; 4.04); smoking (OR 3.46; 95%CI 1.60; 7.50); and not receiving social assistance benefits (OR 2.62; 95%CI 1.28; 5.34). The study found comorbidities and a high prevalence of illicit psychoactive substance use associated with socioeconomic and behavioral health determinants. These data may inform public health management in developing strategies tailored to the specific needs of this population.

papers.title: Factors associated with alcohol and other drug use among transgender people: a cross-sectional study, Espírito Santo, 2022-2024.
papers.abstract: To identify factors associated with alcohol and other drug use among transgender people living in Espírito Santo. This cross-sectional study was conducted with transgender adults using a structured questionnaire. The questionnaire collected sociodemographic and health variables, as well variables on presence of depressive symptoms, quality of life, sleep health and body dissatisfaction. Substance use was assessed using the Alcohol, Smoking and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST). Multivariate linear regression models adjusted for confounding factors were analyzed, with a 5% significance level for all tests. The final sample consisted of 103 transgender people with a median age of 24 years (18-44 years). The drugs with the highest scores and greatest need for intervention were tobacco (45.6%), marijuana (42.7%) and alcohol (32%). Furthermore, approximately 10% of the sample needed intervention for illicit substances. Regression analyses indicated that severity of depressive symptoms, not having undergone gender-affirming surgery, income, education, presence of comorbidities, age, quality of life and smoking were associated with increased consumption of one or more of the substances assessed (p-value<0.050 for all). A significant proportion of participants abused one or more of the drugs assessed. Furthermore, consumption of the substances assessed was associated with multiple social and health determinants, which act intersectionally, reinforcing the vulnerability of this population to drug use.

papers.title: Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis with psychiatric manifestations and choreiform movements: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: To summarize the clinical manifestations, ancillary examination findings, treatment course, and prognosis of a patient with neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis presenting with prominent psychiatric disturbances and choreiform movements, and to review the literature on the clinical spectrum of this disease. A 52-year-old woman with a history of hypertension and biopsy-proven podocytopathy with a "full-house" immunofluorescence pattern showing diffuse positivity for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q, diagnosed in February 2026; however, a definitive diagnosis of lupus podocytopathy remained uncertain, as the patient lacked systemic lupus erythematosus manifestations. She was admitted on April 3, 2026, with a 5-day history of psychiatric disturbances and involuntary choreiform movements in all four limbs, preceded by significant psychological stress (bereavement). Neurological examination revealed slowed responses and impaired calculation. Cranial MRI showed only bilateral periventricular small ischemic foci (Fazekas grade 1) with normal SWI. Initial EEG demonstrated sharp waves and spike-and-wave complexes in the left parietal, occipital, and temporal regions. CSF analysis revealed leukocytosis (21/μl, 90% mononuclear cells), protein of 0.4 g/L, elevated IgG index of 0.76, and elevated 24-hour intrathecal IgG synthesis rate of 5.63 mg/dl. CSF mNGS detected 453 EBV sequences (RPM) with a relative abundance of 97.48%. Serum EBV VCA-IgG and EBNA-IgG were elevated with negative IgM. Autoantibody testing followed a stepwise approach: initial screening for conventional autoimmune encephalitis, paraneoplastic, and demyelinating antibodies was negative; subsequent tissue-based assay (TBA) of CSF revealed strong positive immunoreactivity, prompting expanded antibody panel testing, which ultimately detected anti-neurexin-3α antibodies in serum (titer 1:30) and CSF (titer 1:100), confirmed by both cell-based assay (CBA) and TBA. The patient's condition progressively deteriorated, requiring endotracheal intubation on April 21 and tracheostomy on April 30. She received methylprednisolone pulse therapy at 500 mg/day for 5 days followed by a stepwise taper, intravenous immunoglobulin at 0.4 g/kg for 5 days, and five sessions of plasma exchange from April 30 to May 8 due to poor initial response. Choreiform movements gradually resolved after plasma exchange. She was weaned from mechanical ventilation on May 19 and decannulated on May 27. During the ICU course, she developed pulmonary infection with carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, which was controlled after antibiotic adjustment. Repeat EEG normalized on June 1. She was discharged from rehabilitation on June 9 on oral methylprednisolone 32 mg/day. On June 26, 2026, follow-up serum TBA showed weakly positive immunoreactivity, with the serum antibody titer remaining at 1:30. She subsequently received four infusions of efgartigimod at 400 mg each for consolidation immunotherapy and was transitioned to ofatumumab for long-term maintenance. At follow-up on August 6, 2026, the patient had no residual psychiatric symptoms or choreiform movements, with muscle strength recovered to 4+ in all limbs, full independence in daily activities, ambulation without assistance, and only mild gait instability. Neurexin-3α IgG-mediated autoimmune encephalitis is a rare but treatable condition. Choreiform movements expand its clinical spectrum. The coexistence of podocytopathy raises a hypothesis of shared antigenicity between renal and neuronal neurexin family members, though this remains purely speculative. CSF EBV reactivation may represent a bystander phenomenon or epiphenomenon of severe immune dysregulation rather than a confirmed trigger. Tissue-based assay provides crucial diagnostic direction when conventional screening is negative. Early recognition, comprehensive immunotherapy, and meticulous ICU management are important determinants of favorable outcomes. Given the inherent limitations of a single case report, these findings warrant confirmation through larger cohort studies.

papers.title: A melatonin textile transdermal patch based on physicochemical synergistic permeation-enhancement strategy for circadian rhythm regulation.
papers.abstract: Melatonin, an endogenous circadian rhythm-regulating hormone, has faced challenges in achieving prolonged exogenous regulation due to its low oral bioavailability and short half-life. Existing transdermal strategies are difficult to balance efficacy, safety, and accessibility. To address this, we propose a physicochemical synergistic permeation-enhancement strategy and have developed a melatonin textile transdermal patch based on the synergistic action of electret and permeation enhancer. The patch is designed with a three-layer composite structure, composed of a textile-based electret backing layer, a drug-loading pressure sensitive adhesive layer containing melatonin and permeation enhancer, and a protective layer to prevent drug leakage. Electret and permeation enhancer enhance transdermal efficiency through a physicochemical synergistic permeation-enhancement strategy without disrupting the skin barrier. In vitro studies revealed that among various permeation enhancers (menthol, azone, oleic acid) and electret parameters, the combination of a -1500 V electret with 10% oleic acid exhibited the optimal synergistic effect. In vivo pharmacokinetic studies demonstrated that the patch reached a peak plasma concentration (>30 ng/mL) within 1 h and maintained effective therapeutic levels (>5 ng/mL) for up to 8 h. The patch significantly improved the sleep quality in insomniac rats, with no observed skin irritation or cytotoxicity. This study not only accomplishes an efficient, non-invasive, and parametrically tunable transdermal delivery of melatonin but also validates the feasibility of synergistic enhancement through physical field regulation and chemical permeation, thereby providing a viable strategy for developing safe and long-acting textile-based transdermal drug delivery systems aimed at neuroendocrine small-molecule hormones similar to melatonin.

papers.title: Non-pharmacological traditional Chinese medicine interventions for depression: bibliometric mapping of Chinese databases and WoSCC, 2000-2025.
papers.abstract: The aim of the study was to characterize publication activity, collaboration structures, keyword themes, and temporal changes in the literature on non-pharmacological traditional Chinese medicine interventions for depression. Journal records published from 2000 to 2025 were obtained from CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). Eligibility combined mechanical rules with independent paired assessment of 2,089 boundary records and reference-based reconciliation. The final corpora contained 5,385 Chinese and 721 WoSCC records. Full-counting collaboration and keyword networks were analyzed using weighted Louvain communities, cosine-distance silhouettes, two-state burst intervals, and resolution, seed, Leiden, and terminology sensitivity analyses. Selected graph quantities were cross-checked in R/igraph. Additional checks evaluated record-identity consistency, linkage sensitivity, and annual keyword availability denominators. Chinese output peaked at 390 records in 2021, while WoSCC output reached 118 records in 2025. Complete author networks contained 12,141 Chinese and 2,933 WoSCC nodes and were sparse (densities 0.000410 and 0.003572). Eligible keyword networks contained 569 Chinese and 81 WoSCC terms. Weighted Louvain yielded five Chinese communities (Q = 0.194124; mean silhouette = 0.005173) and four WoSCC communities (Q = 0.134767; mean silhouette = 0.029369). Stability analyses showed only moderate agreement across seeds and alternative algorithms, indicating that the communities are exploratory summaries rather than discrete topic classes. Keyword availability denominators materially altered some WoSCC community time profiles. The literature expanded substantially and centered on acupuncture-related interventions, poststroke depression, evidence synthesis terminology, exercise-based techniques, sleep, and experimental themes. Sparse collaboration networks and overlapping thematic interpretations indicate opportunities for broader collaboration and more consistent terminology. Bibliometric prominence does not establish efficacy, safety, mechanism, or causality.

papers.title: Epilepsy as a consequence of infantile vitamin B12 deficiency: observations from a prospective cohort study and a review of the literature.
papers.abstract: Symptomatic infantile vitamin B12 deficiency has far-reaching neurological consequences for affected children. Development of epilepsy is one such consequence whose incidence and characteristics have been scarcely studied and reported in the literature. To describe the incidence, characteristics, and outcomes of epilepsy in a prospective cohort of children treated for infantile vitamin B12 deficiency and to briefly review the published literature on the topic. A hospital-based prospective cohort study enrolling consecutive children with symptomatic infantile vitamin B12 deficiency was conducted from January 2021 to June 2023 to study the neurological consequences of deficiency. The cohort was followed through March 2026 to determine the incidence of epilepsy during follow-up. Those who developed epilepsy were evaluated for seizure and epilepsy types, neuroimaging and electroencephalography findings, treatment, response to treatment, and outcomes. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling was performed using baseline predictors identified through univariate screening to determine independent associations with epilepsy. A total of 141 children with infantile vitamin B12 deficiency were part of the original cohort. Four died, 25 were lost to follow-up. Among the rest of the 112 children, at a median follow-up of 51 months (IQR: 45-55), 31 (28, 95% CI 19-36%) developed epilepsy. In those with epilepsy, the mean age at diagnosis of infantile vitamin B12 deficiency was 12.39 ± 3.9 months, and epilepsy developed after a mean interval of 4.7 ± 3.2 months after treatment. Epileptic spasms were the most common seizure type (15/31, 48.4%), while other forms of epilepsy were observed in 16. Of the 31, at last contact, 21 (68%) had either resolved or well-controlled epilepsy, 8 (26%) had drug-refractory epilepsy, and 2 (6%) died. In the multivariate model, acute-phase seizures were strongly associated with increased epilepsy risk (pooled HR 4.27, 95% CI:1.6-11.5, p = 0.004). Higher follow-up DQ was protective (pooled HR 0.94, 95% CI:0.89-0.99, p = 0.015). There was an early clustering of epilepsy, with all events occurring within 10 months of follow-up. Epilepsy is a significant neurological outcome of vitamin B12 deficiency in infants. There is early clustering of epilepsy risk after treatment for deficiency, and acute-phase seizures are the strongest independent predictor of later epilepsy.

papers.title: GLP-1/GIP Uptake, Indication, and Access Pathways Among US Adults in the Understanding America Study.
papers.abstract: Evidence on GLP-1/GIP therapies is largely derived from trials enrolling selected populations or medical records that miss utilization outside healthcare channels. No nationally representative cohort has characterized real-world uptake, indications, and access. To characterize GLP-1/GIP prevalence, indication, clinical profile, and access. Prospective cohort study with three GLP-1/GIP surveillance waves (March 2024, December 2024, October 2025). The Understanding America Study, an address-based, nationally representative panel of approximately 15,000 US adults aged 18+ years initiated in 2014. UAS participants responding to at least one surveillance wave (n=9150). GLP-1/GIP use status (never vs any use, comprising current and former use), self-reported primary indication (diabetes, weight loss, or other), and access pathway (traditional vs non-traditional). Survey-weighted prevalence of GLP-1/GIP use, overall and by indication and access pathway; sociodemographic, cardiometabolic, treatment, and access characteristics; and smartwatch-derived resting heart rate, heart rate variability, maximum activity heart rate, step count, and sleep duration and variability. Among n=9150 adults (1274 with any use; 60.9% female; median age 53 years), weighted prevalence increased 46%, from 8.2% (March 2024) to 12.0% (October 2025) representing 32 million. Weight-loss indications grew, reaching nearly half of use (4.1% to 5.6%); diabetes-indicated use was stable (5.3% to 5.4%). Users carried high cardiometabolic burden (obesity, 68.2%; diabetes, 53.6%) but diverged by indication: diabetes-indicated users were older (median, 59 vs 49 years), whereas weight-loss-indicated users were more often female (69.9% vs 51.3%) and healthier. One in three users (~9 million) had non-traditional access, especially in weight-loss-indicated users, of whom 33% had no conventional prescription; 41% used compounding, online, or foreign pharmacies; and, 43% lacked coverage. Non-traditional users were five times as likely to report an unlisted, likely compounded formulation (19.8% vs 4.1%). All p<0.05. Real-world GLP-1/GIP use has grown rapidly and diversified substantially in indication, access, and population profile. One in 3 users obtained treatment through nontraditional channels largely invisible to claims data, raising long-term safety, efficacy, and coverage questions. GLIMMER provides a public, nationally representative longitudinal evidence base for future payer and provider decisions. Question: Who is using glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists or glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptides (GLP-1/GIP) therapies in the US, how has use changed since 2024, and how are these medications obtained?Findings: In this cohort study of 9150 US adults, GLP-1/GIP use rose significantly from 8.2% to 12.0% (March 2024-October 2025), driven by weight loss; those treated for diabetes were a decade older, lower-income, and in poorer health than those treated for weight loss. Overall, 1 in 3 users obtained treatment outside conventional prescribing and dispensing channels.Meaning: A large and growing share of GLP-1/GIP exposure occurs outside the channels visible to claims-based surveillance.

papers.title: Obesity Endotypes Unmask Heterogeneous Responses to Healthy Lifestyle Behaviors.
papers.abstract: Lifestyle interventions are central to obesity prevention and management, yet interindividual variability in response remains incompletely understood. Here, we leveraged genetically defined, distinct obesity endotypes to examine lifestyle-body mass index (BMI) associations across biological pathways. In the UK Biobank, we analyzed 305,713 participants with partitioned polygenic scores (pPSs) representing 10 obesity endotypes. We evaluated interactions between endotype-specific genetic susceptibility and physical activity, diet, sedentary behavior, and sleep on BMI using multivariable linear regression. Primary findings were externally evaluated in the All of Us Research Program using Fitbit-derived lifestyle measures. Favorable lifestyle behaviors were associated with lower BMI for all obesity endotypes, but the magnitude of these associations varied significantly across endotypes. Higher endotype-specific pPSs strengthened the benefits of physical activity (7 endotypes), healthy diet (3 endotypes), nonsedentary behavior (5 endotypes), and adequate sleep (7 endotypes) on BMI. Distinct endotypes demonstrated the greatest responsiveness to different lifestyle domains, with the metabolically unhealthy endotype showing the strongest interaction with physical activity, metabolically healthy endotype with sedentary behavior, hypothalamic dysregulation endotype with diet, and hypoinsulin 2 endotype with sleep, corresponding to differences in BMI of 0.22-0.49 kg/m² between the highest and lowest pPS deciles. These interaction patterns were consistent in the All of Us cohort. Obesity endotypes modify the association between lifestyle behaviors and BMI, demonstrating that responsiveness to lifestyle behaviors is heterogeneous and pathway dependent. These findings provide a framework for precision obesity prevention by identifying individuals who may derive greater benefit from specific lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: Sociodemographic inequalities in sleep duration and quality at 11, 18, and 22 years of age: a cross-sectional study using data from the 1993 Pelotas Birth Cohort, 2004-2015.
papers.abstract: To analyze sleep duration and quality at different ages according to sociodemographic factors. This was a cross-sectional study using data from the 1993 Pelotas Birth Cohort in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, with follow-ups conducted at ages 11, 18, and 22. Sleep duration and quality were self-reported; daily sleep duration was estimated from weekday bedtime and wake-up times, and sleep quality was assessed at 22 years of age using a question about sleep perception. Descriptive analyses were performed, and inequality measures were estimated according to sex, race/skin color, and wealth index. A total of 4,439, 4,081, and 3,800 individuals were analyzed at ages 11, 18, and 22, respectively. Mean sleep duration was 9.7 (95% confidence interval [95%CI] 9.6; 9.7), 8.4 (95%CI 8.3; 8.5), and 8.0 (95%CI 7.9; 8.0) hours. The absolute inequality index at 18 years of age was -1.3 (95%CI -1.5; -1.0) among females and -0.7 (95%CI -1.0; -0.4) among males. At 22 years of age, the proportion reporting "very good" sleep quality was 19.2% (95%CI 17.4; 21.1) among males, while "very poor" sleep quality was 5.2% (95%CI 4.3; 6.2) among females. Sleep duration decreased between 11 and 22 years of age and was longer among females and more vulnerable groups, among whom very good sleep quality was less frequent.

papers.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence.
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a period of distinct maturational changes in sleep physiology. Age-related trends in sleep physiology have been captured using laboratory-based polysomnography, a method limited by logistical burden and high cost. We tested the ability of the Dreem3 sleep EEG headband to replicate established age effects in sleep physiology from late childhood through early adulthood. Typically developing youth (N = 100, 9-26 years) completed 3-4 consecutive nights of at-home sleep recording. We estimated age-related trends across eight macro-architecture and 15 micro-architecture variables with known age effects, and conducted exploratory analyses of 24 additional variables. Dreem3 replicated established age trends, including increases in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) stage 2%, and decreases in N3%, time in bed, NREM delta and theta power with increasing age. Exploratory analysis revealed age effects in twelve additional variables, including decreases in spindle activity with increasing age. Sleep EEG wearables offer an accessible way to characterize sleep physiology development.

papers.title: Sleep dysfunction mediates the relationship between hemodynamic response height of the secondary somatosensory cortex and fear-somatic symptom severity bidirectionally in young adults.
papers.abstract: Background Sleep dysfunction exerts profound effects on cognition and emotion. Among neurophysiological indices, the hemodynamic response height (HRH), as derived from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), represents a key marker of neural activities. Here, we addressed the interplay amongst sleep quality, HRH, and negative emotional states in young adults. Methods We curated fMRI and clinical data of 735 young adults (373 women) from the Human Connectome Project. All participants were assessed for sleep quality with the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and subjective emotional state with the NIH Toolbox of Negative Affect. Imaging data were processed with published routines and evaluated with a corrected threshold. In whole-brain regression we identified regional HRH correlates of PSQI score and, in mediation analysis, assessed the interrelationship amongst the regional HRH, PSQI, and clinical measures. Results With age and sex as covariates, lower HRH in the secondary somatosensory cortex (SII) was associated with higher PSQI score across all subjects. No clusters were identified for hemodynamic time to peak or full width at half maximum at the same threshold. Both SII HRH and PSQI score were significantly correlated with fear-somatic symptom severity. Moreover, mediation analyses showed that PSQI score mediated the relationship between SII HRH and fear-somatic score bidirectionally. Conclusions Reduced hemodynamic responsiveness in the SII is associated with poorer sleep quality and heightened somatic fear symptoms. These findings suggest that sleep dysfunction mediates a bidirectional link between somatosensory activities and emotional dysregulation, highlighting a potential mechanism of affective dysfunction in link with sleep deficiency.

papers.title: Rapid phase resetting of Aedes aegypti circadian rhythms by transient alterations in light exposure.
papers.abstract: Circadian clocks enable mosquitoes to anticipate recurring environmental variations and coordinate behaviors critical for survival and disease transmission, such as locomotion, reproduction, host-seeking, and blood-feeding, with times of day when performance is maximal. In Aedes aegypti , locomotor activity follows a robust diurnal rhythm shaped by endogenous circadian clocks and environmental cues, among which light has been shown to be the primary source of temporal information. While early studies established the role of light in regulating locomotor activity, behavior, oviposition and pupation, it remains unclear which features of a light cycle drive changes in circadian rhythms. This question is increasingly relevant as Ae. aegypti is frequently exposed to artificial and dynamic lighting conditions in urban environments. Here, we investigated how transient changes in light schedules influence circadian rhythms in locomotor activity by systematically manipulating the timing, duration, and direction of light exposure. Using a high-throughput assay, we tested over 1900 individuals, including wild-type and timeless knockout mutants, and showed that a single day of altered lighting is sufficient to induce robust phase shifts, with no evidence of masking effects. A 6-hour light pulse was sufficient to re-entrain mosquitoes regardless of the timing of the pulse, and phase shifts were primarily driven by the offset time of the light pulse, indicating that light-offset acts as a major zeitgeber . Together, these findings challenge conventional assumptions about the timescale of circadian synchronization and highlight the remarkable plasticity of mosquito behavior in response to anthropogenic light. Eventually, these effects could explain the rapid adaptation of the species to urban environments and have potential consequences for disease transmission dynamics. A single day of changes in the light schedule is sufficient to reset the phase of Aedes aegypti 's circadian clock. Circadian phase resetting requires at least four to six hours of light exposure.Advancing the circadian phase is easier than delaying it.

papers.title: CAMSAP3 loss of function models suggest causative role in generalized genetic epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Advancements in next-generation sequencing have led to the discovery of hundreds of human epilepsy gene associations. Newly associated genes require functional validation to establish causation and to inform patient treatment in the clinic. A recent exome sequencing trio analysis identified predicted protein-altering variants in two patients with generalized epilepsy in the gene CAMSAP3 . CAMSAP3 regulates non-centrosomal microtubule dynamics and the acetylation necessary for normal axonal differentiation and migration. We show that overexpression of patient variants leads to protein degradation and dysregulation of microtubule acetylation in cultured HEK cells. Camsap3 knockout zebrafish also exhibit increased axonal microtubule acetylation, as well as epileptic features such as seizure-like swimming behaviors, aberrant inhibitory interneuron development, and epileptiform via electrophysiology. Together, these data suggest that CAMSAP3 plays an important role in genetic generalized epilepsy. Loss-of-function CAMSAP3 variants in individuals with genetic generalized epilepsy alter tubulin dynamics in HEK cells. Camsap3 loss-of-function zebrafish show dysregulation of acetylated tubulin in tectal axon projections. Mutant fish exhibit hyperexcitable swimming behavior, loss of inhibitory interneurons and epileptiform via electrophysiology.

papers.title: Advancing Pediatric Sleep Assessment through Spectral Sleep Scoring: A Comparison with Polysomnography.
papers.abstract: Understanding how sleep changes across development requires methods that are both efficient and sensitive to maturational differences in sleep physiology. Spectral sleep scoring is a promising approach, but has primarily been validated in adult populations. This study presents and validates a spectral scoring approach for pediatric sleep. Participants (n = 192; 9-18y) completed overnight in-lab sleep studies. Visual scoring was determined by registered polysomnographic technologists and confirmed by board certified sleep physicians following AASM guidelines. Visual stages included: wake, non-rapid eye movement (NREM) stage 1 (N1), NREM stage 2 (N2), NREM stage 3 (N3), and rapid-eye movement (REM) sleep. Spectral activity within each epoch was assessed for the following spectral stages: Wake (40-95 Hz), Light (~11- 15.5 Hz), Hi Deep (1-3 Hz), Lo Deep (0.1-1 Hz), and REM (~17-26 Hz). Concordance rates were checked across agreement matrices between visual and spectral stages, with expected high agreement between: 1) visual Wake and spectral Wake; 2) visual N2 and spectral Light; 3) visual N3 and spectral HiDeep/LoDeep; and 4) visual REM and spectral REM. Cohen's κ was calculated from concordance matrices. There was high agreement between visual and spectral stages (71-89%, κ=.76). Our results provide evidence that spectral scoring is a promising method for efficiently scoring pediatric sleep. Moreover, this method provides additional, clinically relevant information that is not readily captured through traditional visual scoring. This may be particularly valuable for assessing sleep physiology in pediatric clinical populations, where developmental differences in EEG patterns may complicate visual scoring.

papers.title: Non-Covalent Poly(ADP-ribose) Signaling Organizes a Circadian E3 Ligase Network in the Brain.
papers.abstract: Although PAR biology has traditionally been studied through covalent PARylation, non-covalent PAR-binding proteins provide an additional mechanism for interpreting transient PAR signals and converting them into downstream regulatory programs. Among these effectors, E3 ubiquitin ligases are uniquely positioned to couple PAR sensing to selective ubiquitination, thereby integrating stress signaling with proteostatic control. Because circadian systems depend heavily on temporally coordinated protein turnover, we hypothesized that PAR-binding E3 ligases may form a circadian-structured regulatory layer within the brain. To test this, we integrated GTEx v10 brain transcriptomics, GWAS Catalog gene-mapped associations, CIRCA circadian phase annotations, and Human Protein Atlas single-cell transcriptomic resources to characterize the organization of PAR-binding E3 ubiquitin ligases across neural tissues. Across the brain, the E3 ligase repertoire was broadly deployed yet regionally structured, with cerebellar and cortical enrichment patterns preserved within the PAR-binding subset. Representative ligases spanning circadian regulation, DNA repair, and neurodegeneration-relevant pathways displayed distinct abundance and regional-variability archetypes across GTEx brain regions. Human genetic analyses demonstrated that E3 ligases associated with cognition-, neurodegeneration-, and sleep/circadian-related phenotypes were disproportionately PAR-binding, supporting convergence between PAR-responsive ubiquitin regulation and disease-relevant biology. Circadian phase analyses further revealed that PAR-binding ligases occupy structured, non-random circadian windows within the broader E3 background, including distinct co-phasing relationships with BMAL1 and CRY1. Finally, cell-type enrichment analyses identified microglia as the dominant compartment for circadian-linked and PAR-binding circadian E3 weighting within the brain E3 program. Together, these findings support a systems-level framework in which non-covalent PAR-binding E3 ubiquitin ligases constitute a brain-deployed, circadian-organized regulatory layer that couples PAR signaling to time-dependent ubiquitin control in neural systems.

papers.title: Effects of Instructional Context on Neural Features of Attention during Learning Activities in Children with and without ADHD.
papers.abstract: Attention is foundational to learning, yet the extent to which features of the instructional environment differentially shape attentional engagement is not well understood. Here we leveraged mobile EEG and video-coded behavioral observation to examine attentional engagement in 6-10-year-old children with and without a diagnosis of ADHD across instructional conditions varying in delivery modality (video watching, online, in-person) and management of learning (teacher-led versus student-led). EEG measures, including alpha-band (8-12Hz) oscillations, spectral slope and offset, and behavioral measures of active engagement (AE%), passive engagement (PE%), fidgeting, off-task behavior, were examined as a function of instructional context. Attentional engagement, as indicated by higher AE%, lower alpha power, flatter spectral slope and lower offset, was greatest in studentled learning, followed by teacher-led in person learning, synchronous online learning, and asynchronous learning, respectively. Child by instructional context interactions revealed that patterns of attentional engagement were largely consistent regardless of diagnosis, with group effects observed for motor behaviors (PE%, fidgeting) but not for measures of visual attention. Similarly, age showed only main effects, whereby older children showed higher passive engagement, lower fidgeting and off-task behavior, flatter spectral slope, and lower offset. The results underscore: (i) the importance of considering environmental context, such as instructional modality and management of learning, when examining mechanisms of attention and individual differences therein, and (ii) the value of recording multiple behavioral and neural measures, as not all indices commonly assumed to reflect attention capture the same underlying processes.

papers.title: Elevated neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility in a mouse model of SCN2A -related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic variants in SCN2A cause a spectrum of neurodevelopmental disorders, including developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE). The patient-associated SCN2A -p.E430A variant selectively shifts voltage-dependence of activation, a mechanism predicted to enhance neuronal excitability. To investigate the functional consequences of the SCN2A -E430A variant, we generated the novel Scn2a E430A mouse model and assessed neuronal excitability, brain activity, seizure susceptibility, and phenytoin responsiveness. Heterozygous Scn2a E430A mice retained normal Scn2a expression levels and did not exhibit premature lethality. Hippocampal pyramidal neurons from heterozygous Scn2a E430A mice were hyperexcitable compared to wild-type neurons. Enhanced long-term potentiation was observed in the CA1 circuit of Scn2a E430A mice. Video-EEG data revealed recurrent epileptiform discharges and spectral abnormalities, but no spontaneous generalized seizure events. In multiple seizure-induction assays, Scn2a E430A mice had no difference in latency to first seizure signs, but exhibited faster seizure generalization and more lethality compared to wild-type mice, indicating alterations in seizure propagation and/or cessation rather than seizure initiation. Pretreatment with phenytoin improved seizure outcomes across all seizure induction methods. Together, these findings demonstrate that selective disruption of Scn2a activation gating is sufficient to drive neuronal hyperexcitability and network dysfunction, establishing the Scn2a E430A mouse as clinically relevant and pharmacologically tractable model of SCN2A -related DEE.

papers.title: Seizures induce c-fos expression in a subset of astrocytes, termed fostrocytes, that dampen subsequent seizures.
papers.abstract: The original goal was to map neuronal circuits activated by spontaneous seizures in models of temporal lobe epilepsy. Studies used the c-fos driven TRAP2 system, which has been used successfully to label neurons after seizures. Unexpectedly, astrocytes were also labeled, then shown to express c-fos in a sustained manner after seizures. The role of these so-called fostrocytes in spontaneous seizures was studied using novel Cre-dependent AAVs. Studies used a homozygous mouse line produced by crossing TRAP2 Cre-driver mice with the Ai9 Cre-reporter line. Seizures were induced using electrical stimulation, kainic acid, or pilocarpine. Cre-dependent AAVs used the GFAP promoter to drive expression of either the catalytic A chain of diphtheria toxin (DTA), GFP, or empty vector. Spontaneous seizures were continuously recorded using EEG. Discrete seizures in naïve mice evoked transient c-fos expression in all astrocytes, while status epilepticus evoked a higher and sustained level of c-fos expression. Timing the activation of the TRAP2 system allowed specific labeling of the subset of astrocytes with high c-fos expression. These cells were colocalized with established astrocyte markers, showed reactive astrocyte morphology, and were selectively labeled by GFAP-driven Cre-dependent AAVs. Ablation of fostrocytes in spontaneously seizing mice increased seizure frequency. Next-generation sequencing studies have revealed a great diversity of astrocyte subtypes, identifying clusters with up-regulated c-fos expression in patients with neurological disorders. In conclusion, these studies suggest that therapies that augment the activity of c-fos expressing astrocytes would have anti-seizure activity. ➢ Discrete seizures triggered a transient expression of c-fos in all astrocytes, while status epilepticus triggered its prolonged expression in a subset of astrocytes.➢ The TRAP2 system expresses inducible Cre recombinase controlled by the Fos gene, providing genetic access to astrocytes that express c-fos at high levels.➢ Cre-dependent delivery of a diphtheria toxin selectively ablated these fostrocytes and exacerbated spontaneous seizures.➢ Novel therapies that augment the activity of fostrocytes are predicted to reduce seizure burden.

papers.title: Systemic hypoxia drives glycogen-fueled progression of lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: In advanced stages, lung adenocarcinoma obstructs airways and disrupts ventilation-perfusion relationships in the lung, causing systemic hypoxemia and enabling a feed-forward loop that accelerates malignancy. Systemic hypoxemia is also experienced due to common respiratory comorbidities such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), potentially accelerating malignancy. In a statewide electronic health record network, pre-existing COPD (598 matched pairs) or sleep apnea (235 matched pairs) independently predicted worse survival following incident lung cancer diagnosis. Since the mechanistic basis of the link between malignancy and hypoxia is not well understood, we created systemic hypoxia in Kras LSL- G12D/+ ;Trp53 fl/fl (KP) mice by delivering low inspired oxygen concentrations (8% inspired oxygen; 8 h daily). Hypoxia nearly doubled tumor multiplicity and selectively remodeled cancer central carbon metabolism. Spatially resolved metabolomics revealed marked tumor-compartment glycogen accumulation, elevated tricarboxylic-acid cycle intermediates, and depleted glycolytic pools. Quantitative proteomics across cellular models and autochthonous tumors demonstrated that systemic hypoxia drives glycogen mobilization selectively through the lysosomal enzyme acid α-glucosidase (GAA). Tumor-cell-autonomous deletion of GAA eliminated the hypoxia-driven growth advantage and disrupted downstream anabolic biosynthetic pathways. Thus, systemic hypoxia drives lung adenocarcinoma expansion by mobilizing lysosomal glycogen reserves through GAA to sustain proliferative growth. Systemic hypoxia acts as an intrinsic driver of lung adenocarcinoma progression.Controlled systemic hypoxia doubles tumor multiplicity and reprograms cancer metabolism.Hypoxic tumors mobilize glycogen via lysosomal GAA independently of HIF-1α stabilization.Tumor-cell-autonomous deletion of GAA eliminates the hypoxia-mediated growth advantage in vivo.Pre-existing COPD and sleep apnea exacerbate hypoxemic burden and worsen clinical survival. Lung tumors compromise pulmonary gas exchange, driving systemic hypoxemia that accelerates malignancy. Comorbidities such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and obstructive sleep apnea compound this hypoxemic burden. Clarke et al. isolate systemic hypoxia in mice, showing it doubles lung tumor multiplicity by inducing glycogen degradation through lysosomal acid α-glucosidase (GAA). Deleting GAA eliminates this hypoxic growth advantage.

papers.title: The Choreography of Coupled Brains: Coordinated Movement and Multi-Scale Neural Synchrony in Musical Theater for Individuals with Developmental Disabilities.
papers.abstract: Performing together, which demands moving, singing, and coordinating in real time, is among the most social things people do, yet whether such coordination synchronizes not only behavior but brain activity, within and between performers, has rarely been examined during genuine performance. In this pilot study, we used mobile electroencephalography, including dual-brain hyperscanning of co-performing partners, to resolve neural change over a 16-week musical-theater program in adolescents and adults with developmental disabilities, the majority autistic. We examined four levels: behavior, spectral power, within-brain (source-space) connectivity, and between-brain synchrony, framing all estimates as effect sizes. Anxiety decreased from pre- to post-intervention, consistently across participant and parent reports. During performance, high-beta and gamma power and within-brain amplitude connectivity rose broadly across the cortex, with maximal effects seen in parieto-occipital regions. Between-brain coupling was similarly carried by amplitude co-fluctuation rather than phase; however, it was graded by the degree of interpersonal movement coordination (strongest when partners mirrored one another) and scaled with movement vigor. Local and within-brain changes were thus broad and state-like, whereas coupling between brains was specific to interpersonal coordination. Coordinated movement may organize neural synchrony across scales, positioning musical theater as a tractable model for studying the social brain in motion.

papers.title: Sensory cortical disinhibition is required for long-term fear memory in humans.
papers.abstract: The transformation of transient threats into enduring memories is fundamental to survival, yet how the human brain constructs long-term fear memory remains elusive. Early sensory cortex, traditionally viewed as a passive feature analyzer, is increasingly recognized as an active participant in fear processing. Here, using a multimodal approach combining high-definition α-frequency transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD α-tACS) with simultaneous EEG-fMRI and transformer-based neural decoding, we tracked fear memory development across early formation, consolidation, and long-term retention stages (assessed at 15 min, 24 h, and 7 days post-conditioning). Spatiotemporal memory representations were evident at all three time points, beginning at an early sensory stage (40-60 ms post-stimulus). Conditioning potentiated occipital α-oscillation desynchronization (a marker of visual cortical disinhibition), which predicted the strength of subsequent long-term memory traces. Critically, targeted α-tACS over early visual cortex induced V1/V2 inhibition, abolished conditioning-potentiated α desynchronization, and selectively disrupted fear-memory consolidation and retention while leaving initial acquisition intact. These findings establish sensory cortical disinhibition as a necessary mechanism for long-term fear memory in humans and identify early sensory cortex as a causal node for interventions targeting persistent maladaptive fear.

papers.title: War exposure, evacuation, and psychological and behavioural outcomes following a large-scale traumatic event.
papers.abstract: Armed conflict may affect civilian mental health not only through direct exposure to traumatic events but also through displacement-related disruption. Following the 7 October 2023, attacks on Israel and the subsequent war, limited evidence has examined the distinct roles of direct war exposure and evacuation in shaping both psychological and behavioural outcomes. To examine the associations of direct war exposure and evacuation with anxiety, depressive symptoms, sleep disturbances, changes in eating behaviour, and weight change among Israeli civilians, and to assess whether younger age and lower pre-war household income show indirect associations with poorer outcomes through evacuation and direct war exposure. Data were collected in March 2025 through a cross-sectional online survey of 513 adults in Israel, including 209 evacuees and 304 non-evacuees. Outcomes included anxiety, depressive symptoms, sleep disturbances, eating-behaviour change, and weight change. Multivariable models and mediation analyses were used to examine the roles of war exposure, evacuation, age, and pre-war household income. Evacuated participants reported higher levels of sleep disturbances, anxiety, and depressive symptoms and were markedly more likely to report changes in eating behaviour and body weight. Eating changes were reported by 62.2% of evacuees compared with 31.9% of non-evacuated participants, and weight stability was substantially less common among evacuees. In multivariable models, direct war exposure was more strongly associated with anxiety, sleep disturbances, and eating-behaviour change, whereas evacuation was more consistently associated with depressive symptoms and weight instability. Younger age and lower pre-war household income showed indirect associations with poorer outcomes through evacuation and/or direct war exposure. Direct war exposure and evacuation were associated with different patterns across the psychological and behavioural outcomes examined. Post-conflict mental health responses should address not only trauma exposure itself but also displacement and socioeconomic vulnerability as important determinants of civilian wellbeing.

papers.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Is Associated With Adverse Short- and Long-Term Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke and TIA: A Retrospective Cohort Study From the Bern Sleep-Stroke Registry.
papers.abstract: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is common after ischemic stroke and has been associated with adverse outcomes, yet evidence from large stroke cohorts remains limited. We evaluated the association of SDB severity with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardio- and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and 3-month functional outcome. This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack admitted to Inselspital Bern between 2017 and 2021 who underwent in-hospital respiratory polygraphy. SDB severity was classified according to the apnea-hypopnea index as mild (5-<15 events/h), moderate (15-<30 events/h), or severe (≥30 events/h). Outcomes included all-cause mortality, first postindex MACCE, and modified Rankin Scale scores at 3 months. Multivariable Cox and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, vascular risk factors, admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, intravenous thrombolysis, and mechanical thrombectomy. Among 1083 patients (mean age, 66.0±14.5 years; 62.6% male), SDB (apnea-hypopnea index ≥5 events/h) was present in 819 patients (75.6%), including mild (29.8%), moderate (22.9%), and severe (22.9%). Median follow-up was 51.1 months (interquartile range, 39.1-67.8) for mortality and 47.7 months (interquartile range, 36.9-65.5) for first postindex MACCE; 178 deaths and 153 of 880 patients experienced a first postindex MACCE. Severe SDB was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.73 [95% CI, 1.04-2.89]). Mild, moderate, and severe SDB were associated with first postindex MACCE (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.78 [95% CI, 1.03-3.06]; 2.20 [95% CI, 1.26-3.84]; and 2.16 [95% CI, 1.23-3.78], respectively; P for trend=0.009). Moderate and severe SDB were associated with unfavorable 3-month functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 1.74 [95% CI, 1.01-3.04] and 2.48 [95% CI, 1.45-4.31], respectively; P for trend <0.001). Severe SDB was independently associated with all-cause mortality, whereas SDB severity was associated with first postindex MACCE and unfavorable 3-month functional outcome. Acute-phase SDB assessment may improve prognostic risk stratification.

papers.title: MAPK15 induces cardiomyocyte senescence and atrial fibrillation by promoting mitochondrial calcium overload via palmitoylating Mcub at the C91 residue.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of atrial fibrillation (AF), particularly age-related AF, is increasing rapidly with global aging. Cellular senescence is a key contributing factor to AF, yet the underlying mechanisms driving atrial cardiomyocyte senescence remain elusive. Although MAPK15 has recently been implicated in regulating epithelial cell senescence, its potential role in the heart remains unclear. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the role of MAPK15 in atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF, and to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We investigated the role and underlying mechanisms of MAPK15 in atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF by cardiac-specific overexpression or knockdown of MAPK15, as well as treatment with small-molecule inhibitors. A combination of transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling, co-immunoprecipitation with mass spectrometry, site-directed mutagenesis, patch-clamp recording, optical mapping and intracardiac electrophysiology was employed both in vitro and in vivo. Findings were further validated using human atrial appendage specimens. Results showed that MAPK15 was closely associated with atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF. Overexpression of MAPK15 aggravated senescence and promoted AF. Mechanistically, MAPK15 induced palmitoylation of mitochondrial calcium uniporter dominant negative subunit b (Mcub) at C91, causing its dissociation from the mitochondrial Mcu complex and translocation to the cytoplasm. This impaired inhibition of mitochondrial calcium uptake, leading to calcium overload, ROS overproduction, and cellular senescence. C91S mutation or palmitoylation inhibition (2-BP) reversed these effects. Subsequently, senescent cardiomyocytes showed increased triggered activity, fibrosis, and altered connexin43 distribution, facilitating AF onset. And serological analysis suggested that IL-17a may act as an upstream regulator of MAPK15. Our findings identify MAPK15 as a novel regulator of atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and AF. MAPK15 promotes mitochondrial calcium overload through palmitoylation of Mcub at C91, highlighting a new mechanistic axis linking mitochondrial dysfunction, cellular senescence, and arrhythmogenesis. Age-related atrial fibrillation is highly prevalent and frequently associated with adverse cardio- and cerebrovascular events, constituting a significant global public health burden. In this study, we demonstrated at both in vivo and in vitro levels that the MAPK15-Mcub axis promotes atrial cardiomyocyte senescence and senescence-associated AF, which was further validated in atrial appendage tissues from clinical patients, enhancing the clinical translational relevance of our findings. Moreover, we identified circulating IL-17a as a potential upstream activator associated with MAPK15 signaling, suggesting its potential utility in preclinical screening and as an insightful clue for future immunomodulatory strategies. The development of small-molecule agents specially targeting MAPK15 or Mcub in cardiomyocytes may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for treating atrial myocyte senescence and AF.

papers.title: The rise of modern tonometry: the evolution of intraocular pressure measurement.
papers.abstract: Intraocular pressure (IOP) is the primary biomarker for the diagnosis and management of glaucoma, a progressive optic neuropathy and the second leading cause of blindness worldwide. Its pathophysiology involves an imbalance between aqueous humor production and drainage that elevates IOP, ultimately damaging the optic nerve. IOP exhibits substantial circadian fluctuations, and single-point clinical measurements frequently fail to capture peak diurnal pressure, thereby underestimating the risk of disease progression, delaying necessary intervention, and obscuring patient compliance with pharmaceutical therapies. This review synthesizes historical, contemporary, and emerging IOP measurement technologies, examining their underlying physical principles, clinical utility, and limitations, with particular emphasis on their capacity to characterize the dynamic, time-varying nature of IOP. The search drew on Google Scholar and manufacturers' websites, focusing on physical principles and systems not yet FDA-approved or clinically tested. A critical unmet clinical need exists for accessible home-monitoring solutions. The ideal device would be non-invasive, affordable, and user-friendly, requiring neither topical anesthesia nor sterilization, and would support remote data transmission to facilitate continuous patient-clinician communication. This unmet need offers an opportunity for engineers and healthcare professionals to develop new technologies to help people avoiding travels to and decongest doctors' offices.

papers.title: Deanna Protocol Ameliorates the Deficits in Human iPSC-Cortical Neurons Carrying Familial Alzheimer's Mutation.
papers.abstract: Deanna Protocol (DP) is an anaplerotic, mechanism-based therapy designed to address impaired cellular energy flux. The present study aims to investigate the effects of DP in treating Alzheimer's disease (AD) by using cortical neurons derived from AD patient iPSCs carrying a PSEN1 mutation, while cortical neurons differentiated from iPSCs of a healthy subject serve as control. PSEN1 cortical neurons were treated with DP acutely (24 h) and chronically (1-3 weeks). The effect of DP was assessed by utilizing TMRE assay for mitochondrial function, immunofluorescent staining for AD neuron morphological pathology, whole cell patch clamp for neuron electrophysiological property, and microelectrode array (MEA) analysis of long-term potentiation (LTP) for neurocircuit function. PSEN1 cortical neurons demonstrated impaired mitochondrial function, elevated pathological biomarkers, reduced neurite complexity, altered electrophysiology, and decreased LTP. DP treatment significantly ameliorated all these phenotypes. This study, while confirming iPSC-PSEN1 cortical neurons as a valid AD model, demonstrated the efficacy of DP on ameliorating structural and functional pathologies in AD neurons. It highlights that targeting energy production could be an effective approach in treating neurodegeneration in AD and suggests its potential efficacy in other neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Early detection of emergent central apnoea in patients on positive airway pressure therapy: A five-year telemonitoring cohort study.
papers.abstract: Treatment-emergent central sleep apnoea (TE-CSA) during positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy is recognised, yet its onset timing and contributing factors remain unclear. This study aimed to ascertain the onset time of TE-CSA via telemonitoring (TM) and identify associated factors. A retrospective cohort of 4,021 obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) patients treated with PAP and monitored via TM from 2017 to 2022 was analysed. TE-CSA was defined as a residual apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) >15 with 50% or more central events. Moreover, if the obstructive apnoea index (OAI) was > 5, patients were excluded. Patients with a central apnoea index (CAI) ≥5 at baseline were excluded. TE-CSA was categorised as transient (<12 weeks), prolonged (12-24 weeks), or persistent (>24 weeks without resolution during the follow-up period). Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed time to TE-CSA onset. A nested case-control study evaluated demographic, cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, sedative use, and PAP treatment type as risk factors. TE-CSA occurred in 171 (4.3%, 95% CI: 3.7-4.9) patients, predominantly prolonged (90.6%), with transient (5.9%) and persistent (3.5%) forms. TE-CSA primarily emerged within the first 60 days of PAP therapy. Multivariate analysis identified older age (Odds Ratio (OR) = 1.03, p < 0.001) and male sex (OR = 2.35, p = 0.003) as significant predictors of TE-CSA development. Telemonitoring detected that TE-CSA onset was most commonly identified within the first 2 months of PAP therapy. Older age and male sex are key predictors. Early detection through TM could facilitate timely interventions, although therapeutic adjustments were implemented throughout the observation period and may have influenced the temporal patterns observed.

papers.title: Gender-specific peculiarities in the manifestation of psychosomatic stress symptoms among law enforcement officers during professional training.
papers.abstract: Aim: To investigate gender-specific peculiarities in the manifestation of psychosomatic stress symptoms and stress levels among cadets during their training and service activities under martial law. Materials and Methods: The research involved 134 (71 men and 63 women) cadets. Psycho-emotional and somatic symptoms of stress, as well as the overall level of stress, were assessed using the test proposed by Yu. V. Shcherbatykh twice: before the 4-week field placement in practical police units and after its completion. Results: It was found that female cadets exhibit more pronounced stress symptoms compared to male cadets, especially after completing their field placements in practical police units. The most pronounced psycho-emotional symptoms of stress in women included anxiety, worry, gloomy mood, difficulty in decision-making; somatic symptoms included pains of an unspecified nature, headaches, low performance, excessive fatigue, and sleep problems. The overall stress level among female cadets was also significantly (p ≤ 0.01) higher after their field placement than among male cadets, by 3.3 points. During the field placement period, the stress level among male cadets increased by 2.5 points (p ≤ 0.05), and among female cadets by 5.3 points (p ≤ 0.001). Conclusions: The research indicates an urgent need to develop stress resilience among cadets, particularly female cadets, during their professional training to ensure the effectiveness of their academic performance under martial law and their subsequent service activities in practical police units, as well as in developing skills to apply available methods for preventing stress-related phenomena during training and service activities.

papers.title: Occupational and Physiological Predictors of Burnout Among Healthcare Workers: The Combined Role of Night Shifts and Sleep Apnea Risk Using Structural Equation Modeling.
papers.abstract: High levels of burnout are common among healthcare workers (HCWs), particularly those who work night shifts. Burnout symptoms may be linked with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), a frequent but often underdiagnosed condition. The association between shift work, risk of sleep apnea and burnout among HCWs was studied. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 400 HCWs (200-night shift, 200-day shift) aged 25-60 years working in different healthcare facilities. Participants completed demographic and occupational questionnaires, the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey (MBI-HSS), and the STOP-Bang questionnaire for risk of sleep apnea. Burnout was defined by MBI-HSS thresholds. Statistical analyzes Chi-square and t-tests, Pearson correlations, and multiple logistic regression were performed. A path analysis with structural equation modeling was used to test for mediation effects of sleep apnea. Night shift workers reported a significantly higher prevalence of burnout (28.5% vs. day shift; p<0.001) with higher emotional exhaustion (30.2 vs. 23.4), depersonalization (12.7 vs. 8.9) and lower personal accomplishment (31.6 vs. 36.3). The proportion of night shift workers was higher at intermediate (39.5%) and high risk (27%) of sleep apnea. Higher prevalence of burnout was related to sleep apnea risk, particularly in night shift workers with high-risk scores (76%). Logistic regression analysis revealed that night shifts, higher BMI, being a nurse and intermediate/high STOP-Bang scores were significant predictors of burnout (p<0.05). Interaction analysis revealed the combined effect of night shifts and sleep apnea on the risk of burnout (AOR = 9.54 for high-risk night shift workers). Correlations also confirmed strong associations between burnout dimensions and both the frequency of night shift and STOP-Bang scores. Independent and synergistic associations of night shift work and increased risk of sleep apnea with higher levels of burnout in healthcare professionals These findings emphasize the need for specific measures addressing sleep disorders and shift scheduling to mitigate risk of burnout in this vulnerable population.

papers.title: Sleep-related disorders and their impact on anxiety and oral health-related quality of life in children during the mixed dentition period.
papers.abstract: To investigate the associations between sleep disturbances, anxiety, and OHRQoL in children during the mixed dentition period. This cross-sectional study included 100 children aged 7-12 years. Sleep disturbances were assessed using the Sleep Disturbance Scale for Children (SDSC), anxiety using the Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders (SCARED) and OHRQoL using the Child Oral Health Impact Profile - Short Form (COHIP-SF-19). Spearman's correlation and multivariable regression analyses were performed. Sleep disturbances were identified in 42% of the participants. SDSC scores were positively correlated with anxiety (rho = 0.43) and OHRQoL (rho = 0.34). In multivariable analysis, anxiety showed independent association with sleep disturbance severity. Sleep disturbances in children are closely associated with anxiety and perceived oral health impacts highlighting the importance of early identification and multidiciplinary management.
